title: Richard Branson’s wife could have survived with crucial medication, coroner finds
summary: A British coroner found Lady Joan Branson's fatal pulmonary embolism could have been prevented with blood thinners after her fall on Necker Island.
story: NASCAR driver Kyle Busch, 41, died from severe pneumonia that escalated into sepsis, his family confirmed. Dr. Cedric Rutland, a pulmonary critical care physician and American Lung Association spokesperson, explains how pneumonia's inflammation and infection can overwhelm the body.
The death of Richard Branson's wife, Lady Joan Branson, could have been prevented if she had received medication to prevent blood clots, a British coroner reportedly found.
Lady Branson died at the age of 80 after being admitted to a hospital in November 2025 after a fall weeks earlier on Necker Island, a British Virgin Island owned by her billionaire husband.
Her cause of death was determined to be a pulmonary embolism caused by deep vein thrombosis (DVT), in which a blood clot travels to the lungs and blocks an artery, the BBC reported.
KIM KARDASHIAN REVEALS NEW HEALTH SCARE WITH HAUNTING CONNECTION TO FATHER'S CANCER DEATH

Senior Coroner Fiona Wilcox told Westminster Coroner's Court earlier this month that Lady Branson did not receive preventive anticoagulants, commonly known as blood thinners, at the hospital despite a "very high risk of developing deep vein thrombosis," according to the outlet.
A British coroner concluded Lady Joan Branson's death likely could have been prevented with preventive blood-thinning medication. (Axelle/Bauer-Griffin/FilmMagic)
According to testimony during the legal inquest, Lady Branson's biggest risk factors included her immobility after a fracture following her fall.
"I do find her death would have likely been prevented, and the lack of anticoagulation did cause or contribute to her death probably," Wilcox said.
COMMON ANTIBIOTIC LINKED TO HIGHER RISK OF DEATH IN ADULTS, MAJOR STUDY FINDS
Wilcox added, however, that the case was not one of neglect because Branson did receive medical care.
The inquest, she said, was to "explore the facts, come to the correct conclusions and learn lessons from this," The Independent reported.
The inquest into Lady Joan Branson's death has drawn attention to the importance of preventing dangerous blood clots in hospitalized patients. (Tim Graham/Sygma/Corbis via Getty Images))

During the inquest, doctors gave differing testimony about whether bleeding risk justified withholding the medication, namely enoxaparin, an injectable blood thinner commonly used to help prevent blood clots in hospitalized patients.
EVERYDAY HABIT LINKED TO DRAMATICALLY LOWER RISK OF DYING FROM HEART DISEASE
The hospital's admitting doctor, Dr. Basir Kunduzi, testified he did not complete a bleeding risk assessment on the day of Lady Branson's admission.
Kunduzi said Lady Branson's death led him to "reflect on [his] role as a doctor" and the importance of "good communication between team members," according to the BBC.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Fox News Digital has reached out to the hospital for comment.
The case highlights the importance of balancing blood clot prevention with bleeding risk when treating hospitalized patients. (iStock)

The findings highlight the lifesaving role of blood thinners, which are often used in hospitals to help prevent DVT in patients who are unable to move normally after surgery, fractures or prolonged bed rest. They can increase the risk of bleeding, however, so doctors must weigh both risks before giving them.

Nearly all hospitalized adults should receive some form of blood clot prevention, either with blood-thinning medication or mechanical devices that help keep blood flowing in the legs, Dr. Jared Ross, a South Carolina-based emergency medicine physician, told Fox News Digital.
"In the vast majority of cases, the benefits outweigh the risks," Ross, who was not involved in the inquest or Branson's care, added.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER
A spokeswoman for Sir Branson said the family does not plan to comment on the inquest and pointed to the numerous social media posts he has made for his wife.
Sir Richard Branson paid tribute to his wife after her death, calling her the "shining star" of their family. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

"Life will never be the same without her," Branson wrote on Instagram last year, calling her the "shining star" of the family. "But we have fifty incredible years of memories — years filled with tears and laughter, kindness, and a love that shaped our family more than words could ever capture. It was a relationship that worked. We just had lots of laughs. We were very lucky."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS
Although pulmonary embolisms can be life-threatening, prompt treatment greatly improves the chances of survival, making early recognition critical.
Symptoms of DVT can include swelling, pain or tenderness, warmth and redness in the affected leg or arm, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

Richard Branson and Joan Templeman married on Necker Island in 1989, the same private Caribbean island where she suffered the fall that preceded her final hospitalization. (PA Images via Getty Images)

A pulmonary embolism, which occurs when a clot travels to the lungs, may cause shortness of breath, chest pain that worsens with deep breathing or coughing, a rapid or irregular heartbeat, coughing up blood, lightheadedness or fainting.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The CDC and the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute say anyone with symptoms of a pulmonary embolism should seek immediate medical attention.
Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

title: Tropical disease spread by mosquitoes claims first recorded death in southern US state
summary: Gay Small died on her 80th birthday from dengue after a mosquito bite near her Tampa home, the Florida Department of Health confirmed Friday.
story: Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious diseases and addiction medicine doctor and associate professor at University of Southern California Keck School of Medicine, discusses the spread, symptoms and management of West Nile virus.
Florida recorded its first confirmed dengue fever death of 2026 earlier this month, according to the Florida Department of Health.

Gay Small of Hillsborough County died Sept. 4 — her 80th birthday — from complications of a dengue infection, including septic shock and multi-organ failure, after she was bitten by a mosquito near her home on Bayshore Boulevard, The Tampa Bay Times reported.

"Cheated. Just, you know, it’s so unfair because she was in good health, and she worked hard to stay healthy, and she walked, and she ate right and, you know, all the things that you’re supposed to do," Small's daughter, Anna Small, told Tampa's WFLA Channel 8.
DANGEROUS MOSQUITO-BORNE VIRUS SPREADS IN ONE STATE AS OFFICIALS WARN OF RISING CASES
"And, you know, this virus just kind of comes out of nowhere. She met the wrong mosquito, and that’s it," Anna Small said.
Small's family said they believe Gay Small first caught dengue years ago while traveling abroad but didn't know it. People who have had dengue before are much more likely to develop severe symptoms.

"While in the hospital, Small said, her mother was weak, her hands turned red and she had trembles that she could hear in her voice," WFLA reported. "She had to go into the ICU by the middle of the week."
A mosquito feeds on human skin. Dengue is spread to people through the bite of an infected mosquito and can cause fever, severe aches, nausea and rash. (iStock)
Small's late husband, Bob Small, spent his career working on dengue vaccines, according to the couple's daughter.
The Florida Department of Health confirmed the death Friday after completing its investigation but did not release additional information, WFLA reported.
The Times, citing University of South Florida public health instructor Kristi Miley, reported that a dengue death had not been recorded in the Tampa Bay area in nearly a century.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral illness that can cause fever, severe aches, nausea, rash and, in rare cases, life-threatening complications, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

The virus is most prevalent in tropical and subtropical regions, including Southeast Asia, the Western Pacific islands, Latin America and Africa. Though less common in the continental U.S., locally acquired cases have been recorded in Florida, California and Texas.

Florida mosquito control agencies have stepped up surveillance, inspections and spraying, as locally acquired dengue fever cases — which means people contracted the illness where they live rather than while traveling abroad — have climbed in recent weeks.
Gay Small’s late husband, Bob Small, spent his career working on dengue vaccines — the same mosquito-borne disease that ultimately claimed his wife’s life, according to reports. (iStock)

The Times reported that, since July, Florida "has been experiencing an unprecedented outbreak of locally caught cases." Hillsborough County, where Small lived, "has been at the epicenter of the epidemic."
Hillsborough and Pinellas counties are under mosquito-borne illness alerts issued by the Florida Department of Health.
"Dengue does not stop at county lines," Pinellas County Mosquito Control Director Alissa Berro told Fox 13.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS
"The mosquitoes that transmit the virus generally stay within a relatively small area, but people travel throughout the Tampa Bay area every day," he said.

"When someone infected with dengue enters a new area, a local mosquito can bite that person and later spread the virus to others. As cases rise across the region, so does the potential for additional local transmission."

In addition to increasing aerial and ground treatments in areas showing dengue virus activity, Hillsborough County Mosquito Management Services has also been inspecting private properties for potential mosquito breeding sites, according to local reports.
Mosquito-control crews across the Tampa Bay area have increased surveillance and treatments as locally acquired dengue cases climb. (iStock)
The increased application of insecticide and larvicide by helicopters appears to be working, the Times reported.
"Of the last 1,500 mosquitoes they've sent for testing, all have returned negative for dengue," it said.

The Florida Mosquito Control Association (FMCA) is urging residents to empty or cover standing water around their homes. The mosquito that spreads dengue is a container breeder, meaning it lays eggs in buckets, planters, plant saucers, tires, discarded toys and other objects that collect small amounts of water, experts say.
The FMCA also advises people to follow what it calls the "three Ds."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Dress in long sleeves, light colors and closed-toed shoes outdoors.Defend with a repellent containing DEET, picaridin, IR3535 or oil of lemon eucalyptus.Dump standing water from containers around the home and check yards regularly.
Dress in long sleeves, light colors and closed-toed shoes outdoors.
Defend with a repellent containing DEET, picaridin, IR3535 or oil of lemon eucalyptus.
Dump standing water from containers around the home and check yards regularly.

Many people infected with dengue have no symptoms, and most people who do become sick recover within a week or two, according to the Mayo Clinic. In some cases, however, the illness can progress to severe dengue, a potentially life-threatening condition.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Warning signs can develop quickly, often within a day or two after a fever subsides. Those may include severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, unusual bleeding or bruising, difficulty breathing, extreme tiredness and irritability or restlessness. People experiencing warning signs of severe dengue should seek immediate medical care.
Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

title: Women turn to testosterone for low sex drive as doctors confront treatment ‘experimentation’
summary: Dr. Kudzai Dombo reveals the insurance denials and dosing guesswork women face seeking testosterone therapy as FDA regulators weigh new access.
story: OB-GYN Kudzai Dombo shares why interest in testosterone is rising among women, what evidence says about libido,and why access, dosing and insurance coverage can be complicated.

When women ask their doctors about taking testosterone to help with menopause symptoms, they can run into insurance rejections, confusing workarounds and dosing guesswork since no testosterone product is FDA-approved for women in the U.S.
On Thursday, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) convened a public workshop to examine the evidence, safety and research gaps with testosterone therapy for menopausal women.

Interest in testosterone therapy has grown as more women seek treatment for symptoms such as low sexual desire, fatigue and reduced quality of life during menopause. Yet the lack of an FDA-approved product has left physicians relying on off-label prescribing and compounded formulations.
MELINDA FRENCH GATES SAYS IT TOOK 3 DOCTORS TO DIAGNOSE THE CONDITION SHE WAS SUFFERING FROM

Dr. Kudzai Dombo, a board-certified obstetrician-gynecologist, Menopause Society-certified practitioner and prescribing physician at Alloy Health, said she sees this dynamic playing out daily at her own Los Angeles practice.
Interest in testosterone therapy has grown as more women seek treatment for symptoms such as low sexual desire, fatigue and reduced quality of life during menopause, doctors say. (iStock)
Once patients get settled on standard estrogen and progesterone regimens, "the immediate next question is, do I need testosterone?" Dombo told Fox News Digital.

Although women may hear about a wide range of potential benefits on social media and from friends, current evidence-based guidelines support testosterone therapy for only one indication: hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD), or persistently low sexual desire.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Clinical evidence supporting its use for energy, mood, bone health or sleep remains limited, though many patients are eager to try it for those secondary benefits, according to Dombo.
The absence of FDA-approved female testosterone products forces patients to rely on compounded creams, over-the-counter purchases abroad or micro-dosed male gels. (iStock)

Because no female-specific formulation exists, doctors must navigate off-label workarounds. They typically choose between using custom compounding pharmacies or micro-dosing FDA-approved male gel packets, which patients must carefully measure out at home.
ALZHEIMER'S RISK MAY BE 35% LOWER WITH COMMON MENOPAUSE TREATMENT, STUDY FINDS

This lack of standardized options creates administrative and financial hurdles. Because the therapy is off-label, insurance routinely denies coverage, forcing clinicians and patients to improvise, a frustration that Dombo experienced firsthand.

"When I was prescribed testosterone, my insurance denied coverage, and my physician recommended a compounded cream to avoid the administrative burden," Dombo recalled. "I said, 'Well, I've already tried compounded, and I actually want to try the gel.'"
"Sexual health is part of your entire health."
Using a discount coupon, she paid out of pocket and discovered that a 10-month supply of male gel packets was actually cheaper than a single month of compounded cream.
"It's just an example, I think, of how we have to adapt to a system that has not supported patients when it comes to access to testosterone therapy," she said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Dosing male products can also present clinical challenges. Dombo described a patient in her private practice who precisely measured out one-tenth of a male gel packet daily using a syringe.
Despite three months of consistency, follow-up bloodwork showed no change in hormone levels, and the patient experienced no symptom relief.
Rising advocacy from patients and medical professionals has pushed federal regulators to officially evaluate standardized access and scientific evidence for female testosterone therapy. (iStock)

"We're left to kind of decide, 'Well, what now?'" Dombo said. "It's all experimentation. ... We don't have a set guideline for how to be able to do this for women. We have to rely on the art of medicine."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
The latest federal meeting represents a critical step forward, according to Dombo, who believes grassroots advocacy from patients and clinicians is forcing regulatory action.
"We're not going to stop knocking on the door because there are several of us who believe that women deserve to be able to have access to just what they need," she said.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Sexual health is part of your entire health," Dombo emphasized, expressing optimism that regulatory agencies will eventually adapt to support safer, standardized access.
Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

title: Supreme Court blocks Missouri from using new congressional map in 2026 election
summary: The Supreme Court ordered Missouri Friday to use its 2022 congressional map for the 2026 election, blocking use of the state's newer 2025 map.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

The Supreme Court on Friday ordered Missouri to use its 2022 congressional map in the 2026 election, blocking the state from using a newer map that could have benefited Republicans in the upcoming midterm elections.The unsigned order drew no noted dissents, with the justices making clear that lower courts should neither prohibit use of Missouri’s 2022 map nor require the state to use the 2025 map.
"The District Court and Court of Appeals should not enjoin or otherwise prohibit the use of the 2022 map in the 2026 congressional election in Missouri," the order states.
MISSOURI'S REDISTRICTING MESS CREATED AN ELECTION PROBLEM SUPREME COURT HAS DAYS TO UNTANGLE

People gather at the Missouri statehouse in Jefferson City, Mo., to protest the legislature's efforts to change the state's congressional district maps. (Tammy Ljungblad/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images, File)

"And the District Court and Court of Appeals should not order or otherwise require Missouri to use the 2025 map in the 2026 congressional election in Missouri."The ruling effectively ends the immediate legal wrangling over which congressional map Missouri will use for the 2026 election, leaving the older boundaries in place.The Supreme Court ordered Missouri to use its 2022 congressional map for the 2026 election rather than the state’s newer 2025 map.

title: Florida GOP nominee blasts 20-year Dem incumbent as a 'socialist' rubber-stamp with 'precious little to show'
summary: Former Florida legislator Mike Beltran seeks to oust 10-term incumbent Kathy Castor in 14th district, arguing she has been ineffective and out of touch with constituents.
story: The FL-14 GOP hopeful takes aim at the 10-term incumbent's record, accusing her of empowering radical policies and refusing to debate ahead of November.

Calling out federal waste and foreign aid subsidies while pointing to his own record of bucking party leadership in Tallahassee, GOP 14th congressional district nominee Mike Beltran promises to bring a sharp litigator’s cross-examination to Washington’s budget crisis.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital detailing his bid to unseat 20-year Democratic incumbent Kathy Castor, the former Florida state representative laid out a case rooted in strict fiscal accountability, pledged to challenge even Republican leadership on bloated federal budgets, and warned of the Democrats' embrace of socialism.
(Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
HOUSE CONSERVATIVES UNLEASH MULTIMILLION-DOLLAR MIDTERM BLITZ AGAINST DEM 'SOCIALIST' INSURGENCY
Beltran argues that despite her lengthy tenure on Capitol Hill, the people of Tampa Bay have not been served well by Kathy Castor.

"People in Tampa Bay have precious little to show for Kathy Castor's two decades of incumbency. She's had no major legislative initiatives. All she's really done is rename post offices. And all that's likely to happen if we reelect her is for her to rename every post office from Tampa to Timbuktu.

"She votes with her party over 90% of the time, including radical socialists. She voted in lockstep with Nancy Pelosi and she's poised to elect the Speaker Hakeem Jeffries. And Speaker Hakeem Jeffries would appoint a Chair Raskin, a Chair Omar, a Chair Cortez, and those folks would push radical policies in Congress that are completely out of line with what Tampa families need."
Beltran argues that in the Florida Legislature he served as an independent conservative voice, not automatically beholden to party leadership, and pledges to continue that approach in Washington.

"I've had the courage to vote against special interests even when my own party had lost its way. I've voted against insurance companies, home builders, trial lawyers, I voted against various special interests…whenever somebody was doing something that wasn't good for Tampa families.

"And I had that bipartisan record throughout my time, starting in 2019 and continuing through to 2024, unlike my opponent who discovered bipartisanship merely weeks ago. So I'm always going to do what's best for the communities that I represent, regardless of party, regardless of special interests, regardless of pressure. And that's what I'm proud of, having that independent voting record."

Rep. Kathy Castor, D-Fla., takes her seat for the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party hearing in the Cannnon House Office Building on Tuesday, January 30, 2024.
Beltran argues that the United States needs to reexamine its military and geopolitical relationships, with an eye to fiscal prudence:

"It cannot be a one-sided exchange. You cannot have a wealthy country like Germany spend under 2% of GDP on their military when we're spending over 5% of our GDP on our military budgets, about a trillion dollars. And a lot of that is spent overseas protecting other wealthy countries.

"You see Ukraine and Israel, they're defending themselves from their adversaries. They're doing a good job of that. But we are borrowing $2 trillion a year from countries like China. And that's causing inflation. And what that says is that we don't have money to be sending, particularly to wealthy allies like Germany and Spain.

"These are countries where we have bases, where we've had trouble getting basing privileges or overflight rights for the conflicts that we do need to engage in. And we shouldn't be subsidizing them anymore.

"You see Israel spends over 10% of GDP on defense, as does South Korea. Those countries are carrying the weight of their own defense, but we don't see that from all of our NATO allies. And they're a lot closer to these rogue states, to these conflict regions than we are. They should be doing more, and they're doing less, and that's unacceptable."
As an attorney, Beltran makes the case that he will bring a strong skill-set to Capitol Hill, to do away with business as usual and to fight for the citizens of Hillsborough County:
The US Capitol in Washington, DC, US, on Sunday, May 18, 2025. (Alex Wroblewski/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"My legal skills are quite good. I'm a good cross examiner. I'll be good at scrutinizing witnesses who come before committees that I serve on. I've litigated in the federal courts, so I know the federal statutes. I know issues that need to be redressed. I know how to write statutes so that they can be easily applied by judges, so that attorneys can counsel their clients on what the law is and what they need to do to comply with that.
"I'm proud to be a practicing attorney. I've helped a lot of businesses and individuals throughout Tampa Bay for almost 20 years.
FIRST DATA CENTER BILL CLEARS HOUSE AS BOTH PARTIES SCRAMBLE FOR ANSWERS ON AFFORDABILITY

"And my opponent is also an attorney, but she hasn't practiced in a very long time. She was, I think, a land use attorney, she says, before she was a county commissioner. But I don't think she brings that same skill-set. I've never seen her cross-examine a witness to any effect. And I haven't seen her apply her legal skills to any legislative initiative. In fact, it's kind of difficult to identify anything that she's enacted that's of any particular value to Tampa or otherwise."
Kathy Castor has repeatedly voted against the interests of ordinary Americans in Florida's 14th district, Beltran argues:
"Well, she opposed tax cuts for the middle class and working class and retirees. She opposed removing taxes on tips, removing taxes on Social Security, removing taxes on overtime.

"And she wanted to pay, through taxpayer funds, for trans surgeries for children. And that was a very recent vote. That wasn't something that we have to reach into ancient history to find. And I opposed that.
"I see no reason why a single mother here in Hillsborough County should be paying taxes to pay for trans surgeries for minors while she actually is being taxed on her overtime or her tips."

title: WATCH: DHS issues stark warning after 300 ‘hostile’ cartel drones detected at southern border
summary: The Department of Homeland Security warned cartels their drones are failing as 378 were detected at the southern border in just over one month.
story: Fox News correspondent Max Gorden reports from Yuma, Arizona, where U.S. Border Patrol is deploying advanced counter-drone technology to detect and disrupt cartel drones as officials respond to evolving security threats along the southern border.
The Department of Homeland Security issued a stark warning after more than 300 cartel drones were detected along the southern border in just over a month.

According to the Department of War, 378 cartel drones were detected at the southern border between Aug. 22 and Thursday. Of those, 75 drones were turned back, 15 were engaged and one was captured. Fox News Digital previously reported that the War Department’s Joint Task Force – Southern Border took down "approximately" 100 suspected cartel drones in August alone.

In response to the threat, the Department of War and DHS are increasing their use of drone detection and interception tools along the southern border. The agencies are also working with private companies to develop technology to counter the increased presence of cartel drones.
In a statement posted on X, DHS wrote that "hostile surveillance of American personnel ends here."
EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP’S CBP AXES BIDEN-ERA POLICY ALLOWING PRIVATE GIFTS FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IN FEDERAL CUSTODY

Army Sgt. Drew Scheffer, right, assigned to Joint Task Force Southern Border, provides surveillance over the southern border near Santa Teresa, N.M., on April 12. The military has been patrolling the southern border as part of the Trump administration’s crackdown on illegal migration. (iStock; Department of Defense)
"To the Cartels," DHS wrote, "Your drones are failing, your tactics are being exposed, and you have no advantage. @CBP and @DeptofWar will keep taking them down."

In an interview with Fox News, Jeffrey Stalnaker, deputy chief patrol agent for Border Patrol, said cartels primarily use drones for reconnaissance during drug and human smuggling operations rather than for smuggling.
Cartels previously sent lookouts to monitor Border Patrol agents and other U.S. personnel but now use drones to watch from overhead.

"They’re watching when our soldiers and our agents are coming into the field, where they’re working, and then that allows them to plan how they’re going to send individuals north from Mexico into the United States illegally, trying to circumvent us between the ports of entry," he explained.

Federal officials told Fox News that U.S. anti-drone measures at the southern border have succeeded so far, but cartel drone tactics are rapidly evolving. Some cartel drones are known to be used for lethal purposes, but officials said those have not yet been encountered at the border. For the past three weeks, the U.S. military has been conducting exercises in the desert outside Yuma, Arizona, testing new anti-drone gear ranging from guns and unmanned aerial vehicles to drone-capturing technology.

A U.S. Army Stryker armored vehicle guards the U.S.-Mexico border in El Paso, Texas, on July 7, 2025, after the establishment of a 260-mile military zone along the southern border in New Mexico and Texas.  (Reuters/Jose Luis Gonzalez)

Brigadier General Jason Rueschhoff, director of operations for U.S. Northern Command, told Fox News, "We are developing capability at a pace that is keeping ahead of our enemy, and that's really important. And that's what happens here."

Fox News Digital reported at the start of the month that Joint Task Force – Southern Border was carrying out drone takedowns using specialized counter-drone equipment provided and integrated by other military units, according to a senior War Department official.

The official said each operation was planned and closely coordinated with the Mexican military and border authorities to prevent interference or unintended conflicts between forces operating on either side of the border.

title: As Singham faces federal probe, wife marches in anti-Israel protest led by groups he funded
summary: Jodie Evans, wife of tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham, marched alongside People's Forum activists in a four-hour anti-Israel protest through Manhattan.
story: Fox News Digital's Asra Nomani spoke with Jodie Evans during a New York City protest that took place while Israeli Prime Minister Bibi Netanyahu delivered remarks at the United Nations General Assembly.

NEW YORK — A network funded by Neville Roy Singham, a communist tech tycoon living in Shanghai, mounted a coordinated anti-Israel protest through Midtown Manhattan Thursday after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the United Nations, deploying field marshals, pre-made signs, banners, megaphones, drums, portable sound equipment and a stage for a four-hour demonstration.

At 3:40 p.m. Thursday, field marshals and foot soldiers from the People’s Forum Inc. connected to their "comrades" in the Singham network at the steps of the New York Public Library on Fifth Avenue. Fox News Digital watched the operation unfold from setup to breakdown.

At the center of the protest was Jodie Evans, Singham’s wife, a longtime leader at the People’s Forum and the co-founder of CodePink — a nonprofit that has operated within the broader pro-communist activist network funded by her husband. As Fox News Digital first reported, the Justice Department's U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York opened a grand jury investigation into alleged money laundering, bank fraud and wire fraud by Singham and his network. Singham and the organizations he has funded haven't been charged with any crimes.

As the march moved through Manhattan, self-declared "comrades" of the Revolutionary Communists of America chanted, "Long live the intifada," while Evans and activists from other organizations within the Singham network marched alongside members of the Democratic Socialists of America.
"Intifada! Intifada! Long live the intifada!" the crowd shouted, chanting the term used by Palestinian militants to violently oppose the existence of the state of Israel.
FROM AUSTIN TO NEW YORK, PRO-CHINA NETWORK FUELS WEEK OF ANTI-US PROTESTS AS XI MEETS TRUMP

CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans marches at an anti-Israel protest in New York City alongside a file photo of her husband, Shanghai-based tech entrepreneur Neville Roy Singham. (Left: Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital; Right: Dave Kotinsky/Getty Images for V-Day)

Earlier, police arrested actress Susan Sarandon, a regular speaker at People’s Forum events and protests, after demonstrators blocked First Avenue in an anti-Israel sit-in. CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin and actress Cynthia Nixon were also among the protesters. The demonstration included activists from Jewish Voice for Peace, another partner of the Singham network whose leaders have advocated replacing Israel with a state called "Palestine."

By the end of the evening, at 8:08 p.m., Fox News Digital observed the protesters rolling their carts back to the People’s Forum Inc., the network’s Midtown headquarters on W. 37th Street and a key organizing hub for the Singham network’s street demonstrations on issues from Israel to anti-American tech. Congressional lawmakers, the Justice Department and federal, state and local policymakers have criticized the groups as antisemitic, anti-American and "Trojan horses" for the Chinese Communist Party.
WATCH: Revolutionary Communists of America march at anti-Netanyahu protest in NYC

The day’s events, documented in real time by a Fox News Digital investigative team, provided a rare, on-the-ground view of the infrastructure behind the network’s protests. The operation involved assigned marshals, paid nonprofit staff, pre-made signs, portable sound equipment, rolling wagons, a stage, coordinated slogans and a media team producing content for online distribution.

While not every group participating in the demonstration was directly funded by Singham, the personnel and logistics showed how organizations with overlapping leadership, funding and messaging can operate together to turn a political flashpoint into a professionally-managed street campaign.
WATCH: Singham-linked Party for Socialism and Liberation activists roll in stacks of protest signs at Bryant Park
SOCIALIST, COMMUNIST GROUPS COORDINATE, PROMOTE 'SPONTANEOUS' ANTI-ICE PROTESTS IN AUSTIN

The appearance of Singham’s wife alongside leaders and activists from the People’s Forum, BreakThrough News, the Party for Socialism and Liberation, the Palestinian Youth Movement and a "Shut It Down for Palestine" campaign provides visible evidence of the Singham network’s central role in organizing and promoting anti-Israel protests, particularly in the aftermath of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attacks on Israel.

The coordinated signage and equipment revealed an organizing and logistics infrastructure that moved people, messaging and materials through the city for three hours. Fox News Digital has observed the same materials at a number of separate protests, targeting not only Israel but rallying support for the Islamic Republic of Iran, the communist regimes of Venezuela and Cuba, and fighting data centers and American AI. That infrastructure helps explain how the same network has repeatedly transformed breaking news and political flashpoints into large, highly-coordinated anti-Israel protests across the country.

The protest’s visible organization reflected the scale of the financial network behind some of its leading participants. After his wedding to Evans in 2017 and the sale of ThoughtWorks, the technology company he founded, Singham directed $285 million to nonprofits and media organizations, according to a Fox News Digital investigation. The People’s Forum received $22.4 million from Singham, while CodePink received $1.33 million. BreakThrough BT Media Inc., which operates BreakThrough News, received $1.098 million, according to tax filings.
POWER COUPLE OF CHAOS: HOW A TYCOON AND ACTIVIST BUILT A 'REVOLUTIONARY BASE' AT THE HOUSE OF SINGHAM

On Feb. 14, 2018, Jodie Evans, co-founder of CodePink, and Neville Roy Singham, founder of Thoughtworks, attend V20: The Red Party, a 20th anniversary celebration of V-Day and The Vagina Monologues, featuring a performance by playwright Eve Ensler and an after-party at Carnegie Hall in New York City. (Dave Kotinsky/Getty Images)
DOJ LAUNCHES GRAND JURY PROBE INTO MARXIST MOGUL NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S FUNDING OF LEFTIST GROUPS

In his United Nations address, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called the demonstrators "phony human rights protesters" who have been silent in speaking out against atrocities by the Islamic Republic of Iran against its citizens.
Evans’ presence also offered an unusually direct view of the people behind the anti-Israel protest machine that has mobilized repeatedly across New York and other American cities against Israel.

At about 4 p.m., Manolo De Los Santos, executive director at the People’s Forum, arrived and moved near the anti-Israel signs his foot soldiers had rolled onto the steps of the New York Public Library. A lieutenant handed out signs calling for sanctions against Israel and declaring, "WAR CRIMINALS NOT WELCOME" and "NEW YORK REJECTS ZIONISM." At the bottom, the signs carried the branding of a communist group that the People’s Forum works with closely: the Party for Socialism and Liberation, which doesn’t publicly disclose its finances.

Beside De Los Santos stood Layan Fuleihan, a controversial fixture in anti-Israel protests. Fuleihan, a Palestinian American, spoke at an Oct. 8, 2023, protest that the People’s Forum organized, supporting the Hamas attack on Israel and saying, "Yesterday, the world woke up to incredible news. The media will tell you that yesterday, terrorists invaded Israel. But we know that actually what happened is that the oppressed people of Palestine broke out of the open-air prison they have been subjected to."

People’s Forum posted the video on its own X account. In the same video, De Los Santos declared, "If you listen to the media in this country, you will think the war started 48 hours ago. We know this war started 75 years ago," with the birth of the state of Israel. Fuleihan didn’t reply to questions from Fox News Digital.

People’s Forum executive director Manolo De Los Santos, left, and Layan Fuleihan, right, attend an anti-Netanyahu protest at Bryant Park in New York City on Sept. 24, 2026. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)

Taher Dahleh, center, an organizer with the Palestinian Youth Movement, takes a cigarette from a Winston Blue box while speaking with activists outside the New York Public Library ahead of an anti-Israel protest in New York City on Sept. 24, 2026. At left is People’s Forum Education Director Layan Fuleihan. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)
REPORT: CHINESE PROPAGANDA, SINGHAM NETWORK, FOREIGN DARK MONEY LINKED TO CAMPAIGNS AGAINST DATA CENTERS

The demonstration also showed the role of paid personnel in the network’s street protest operations. Fuleihan was paid $78,649 as the People’s Forum’s education director, while David Chung, the organization’s organizing director, earned $76,249, according to the nonprofit’s latest IRS filings. Their presence alongside field marshals, volunteer coordinators and campaign organizers showed an operation with designated personnel responsible for recruitment, messaging, crowd movement and event logistics.

Nearby, towering over many of the protesters, Taher Dahleh, an organizer with another partner of the People’s Forum — the Palestinian Youth Movement — moved through the crowd, grabbing a Winstone Blue cigarette from another activist, directing demonstrators and coordinating the march. He has been a familiar presence at anti-Israel demonstrations since Oct. 7, 2023, regularly hosting volunteer meetings on Monday nights at the People’s Forum for a campaign called "Shut It Down For Palestine." During the "March on Washington to Let Gaza Live!" that People’s Forum co-organized in November 2025, Dahleh slammed "tech companies" for allegedly contributing to the "slaughter" of Palestinians by selling services to the government of Israel.

Between late 2023 and late 2024, far-left nonprofit WesPac Foundation Inc. gave Palestinian Youth Movement $1 million through its nonprofit fiscal sponsor, Honor the Earth, according to tax filings. Records show it’s received funds from several other sources over the years. The Palestinian Youth Movement still shares a post on its Facebook page from years ago, quoting a young Palestinian killed after murdering three Israelis: "You who possess arms and bullets, remember that there is an enemy so that you may put your bullets in their bodies, not the bodies of your own people." Dahleh didn’t respond to a request for comment.
HOUSE PANEL SUBPOENAS 3 LEFT-WING GROUPS IN PROBE OF $39M TIED TO MARXIST TYCOON NEVILLE SINGHAM

The protest followed a familiar playbook that Evans, De Los Santos, Fuleihan, Dahleh, Chung, the People’s Forum and the Singham network have used since Oct. 7, 2023, to mobilize students at Columbia University, launch a campus encampment and storm Grand Central Terminal. Since then, the same constellation of communist, socialist and anti-war groups has repeatedly turned out for protests over Israel, ICE, the Trump administration, the war against the Islamic Republic of Iran, the arrest of Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro and other political flashpoints — including protests against U.S. data centers, American AI, and U.S. technology companies like Palantir Technologies, Microsoft and Google.

This time, Dahleh and People’s Forum field marshals led the activists from the steps of the public library on Fifth Avenue to E. 42nd Street, where they headed eastbound toward the United Nations past Grand Central Station. Inside the crowd, the network’s social media operation made the march seem like a spontaneous display of mass public anger. At 5:20 p.m., with the march still in force, People’s Forum posted a tightly-cropped video on X, showing demonstrators streaming below flapping American flags with a caption celebrating a "massive crowd of protesters taking to the streets demanding war criminal Netanyahu be brought to justice! Free Palestine!"

However, outside the limited mile-long path of the march, New Yorkers went about their ordinary days. The repeated appearance of the same organizations, leaders, signs, sound systems, wagons and protest infrastructure rolling through the streets of New York City revealed the professional organizing system operating behind the scenes, not a "massive crowd."
WATCH: Neville Roy Singham’s wife Jodie Evans appears at anti-Israel protest, denies he funds protest efforts

On E. 42nd Street, Evans — Singham’s wife and a central figure in the network surrounding the People’s Forum and other Singham-funded organizations — smiled widely as she kept step with the activists, marching behind the bright yellow-and-black signs marked "Party for Socialism and Liberation."
Evans marched with CodePink activists behind a large "STOP ARMING ISRAEL" banner and carried a poster depicting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as "WANTED" for "GENOCIDE."
Evans stood out in trademark CodePink colors, wearing an oversized fuchsia hat, pink peace-sign earrings, dark glasses, a pink-and-white keffiyeh and a shirt reading "I ♥ Palestinian Human Rights."
Her appearance placed a member of the financier’s immediate family directly in the middle of the protest activity his money has helped sustain.

When Fox News Digital asked her about her husband’s funding for nonprofits leading anti-Israel protests, she didn’t answer the question directly and responded, "He’s not been in the United States for six-and-a-half years."
When asked about his position on the protests, she answered: "He supports stopping a genocide, you bet."

Evans laughed off questions about Singham backing the Chinese Communist Party. In a video that Fox News Digital unearthed, Singham stood at the Golden Tulip Hotel in Shanghai during a November 2025 conference and expressed support for "a new world order that is based on multilateralism that President Xi and the CPC [Communist Party of China] and China have proposed."

Jodie Evans, co-founder of CodePink and wife of Neville Roy Singham, was seen helping lead a coordinated anti-Israel protest in Manhattan as Fox News Digital tracked the demonstration from start to finish. (John Taggart for Fox News Digital)

CodePink co-founder Jodie Evans marches during an anti-Israel protest in New York City on Sept. 24, 2026, alongside members of the Revolutionary Communists of America and a hammer-and-sickle flag. (John Taggart/Fox News Digital)

On Sept. 24, 2026, over about four hours, professional protest organizers from the People's Forum, headquartered on W. 34th Street in midtown Manhattan, led anti-Israel activists along a one-mile route from the New York Public Library on E. 42nd Street to the United Nations to protest Israel. At the protest's end, they backtracked and moved to a rally in Time Square before wheeling their signs back to their headquarters on W. 34th Street. (Fox News Digital)
LAWMAKERS THROW OUT 'TROJAN HORSE' ACTIVISTS THEY SAY ARE ENGAGED IN AMERICAN SUBVERSION
Evans denied allegations from lawmakers on the House Foreign Affairs Committee that the Singham network acts as a "Trojan horse" for the Chinese Communist Party, calling them "a lot of lies."
"We're not doing anything wrong. So it's a lot of ‘alleging,’ and we're very honest about what we do: protesting every day," she said. "That's what we do. And that's what I've done for 55 years."

She got visibly agitated on the topic of China. "China is not our enemy!" she said. "That's the message. You know what? I've been going to China for six and a half years. I can't talk about China. It's complex. I don't understand it. I'm just trying to learn about it. So it's not about China. It's about the United States not using our tax dollars to go to war on China. There's never an excuse to go to war on people."

The protest was also packaged for online amplification. During the march, Zoe Alexandra, news editor of BreakThrough News, moved through the crowd conducting interviews, pulling Danaka Katovich, national co-director of CodePink, away from Evans’ CodePink contingent for a chat. BreakThrough later posted a branded one-minute, 21-second video on X under the headline: "Thousands protest…" Singham gave $1.098 million to Breakthrough BT Media Inc., which operates BreakThrough News, according to tax filings.
SINGHAM-LINKED NONPROFITS FIGHT HOUSE SUBPOENAS, ACCUSE LAWMAKERS OF MCCARTHY-ERA ‘WITCH HUNT’

The protest featured black-and-white keffiyehs, a torched effigy of Netanyahu, bloodied cardboard imagery of Netanyahu and Arabic chants declaring that "Israel will be Arab." Critics say the slogans and imagery go beyond criticism of Israeli policy, invoking violent resistance and portraying the elimination of Israel as a political objective.

To close out the protest near the United Nations, a leader from the Singham network manned the pop-up stage with a black-and-white keffiyeh over his shoulders, his arms tightly crossed, as speakers blasted the U.S. and Israel. As their last speaker, organizers returned to another leader from the People's Forum, Tajee Bounds, who serves as membership, events and volunteer coordinator.

A graduate of Columbia University, Bounds was in the middle of the campus’s first encampment in April 2024 with People's Forum organizers when he stood, holding a banner and yelling along with a chant: "Up, up with liberation! Down, down with occupation!" The Columbia Spectator posted a video with his proclamation.
People’s Forum Membership, Events and Volunteer Coordinator Tajee Bounds speaks during an anti-Israel protest in New York City on Sept. 24, 2026. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)
"Glory, glory to our martyrs," an activist chanted, before Bounds took the microphone at 6:31 p.m. to lead the crowd in a chant: "Gaza! Gaza! You will rise!"

At 7:01 p.m., People’s Forum activists began rolling away their wagon full of yellow-and-black signs, set upside down, declaring, "ARREST WAR CRIMINAL BENJAMIN NETANYAHU!" Bounds and others began breaking down their stage and speaker system.
HOW CODEPINK CO-FOUNDER MEDEA BENJAMIN'S FAMILY FOUNDATION BECAME A MAJOR FUNDER OF LEFT-WING ACTIVIST GROUPS

For a dramatic backdrop, the protest moved west on 42nd Street to Times Square, like so many protests have ended before. There, CodePink's Benjamin, Evans' fellow co-founder and a guest at Singham and Evans’ wedding in 2017, created a video for Instagram with herself standing in front of the protesters wearing a black-and-white keffiyeh scarf and narrating to the camera the day's events: "These protests against Netanyahu and the Israeli regime have been going on since 10 a.m. All day long! Now it’s nighttime!"
CodePink’s message throughout the video repeated the mantra of the day’s protest: "FROM THE RIVER TO THE SEA PALESTINE WILL BE FREE."

The videos presented the demonstration as a spontaneous eruption of grassroots anger. But the footage was the product of the same operation it portrayed: professional organizers supplied the signs, sound equipment, rolling carts, stage and coordinated messaging, while BreakThrough News, People’s Forum and CodePink activists recorded and distributed footage from the event. The sequence created a feedback loop in which organizers built the spectacle, captured it on video and circulated the images as evidence of the movement’s scale and momentum.

Protesters display signs from the Maoist Communist Union and Spartacist League during an anti-Israel demonstration in New York City on Sept. 24, 2026. One sign reads "Ansar Allah Don’t Miss" and "Victory to the people! From Maoist Communist Union," while another criticizes the Democratic Socialists of America and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. (Asra Q. Nomani/Fox News Digital)

After the Times Square theater, foot soldiers for the People’s Forum rolled their wagon back onto W. 42nd Street, past the Port Authority and a McDonald’s on Eighth Avenue, with their trademark bright yellow-and-black signs. Others carried the bloodied cardboard imagery of Netanyahu and other protest paraphernalia.
They ended up at the hub of the anti-Israel activist, the headquarters of the People’s Forum on W. 34th Street, carrying signs past books by communist leader Karl Marx and other ideologues.
Inside the People’s Forum's large meeting hall, Chung, organizing director of the People’s Forum, awaited the returning protesters.
De Los Santos greeted them at the door, stepping outside to tell Fox News Digital that he was proud of the group’s work leading the anti-Israel protests for the past three years.
"We organize protests. What is wrong or illegal about that?" De Los Santos said, as his workers drew the shades on the People’s Forum.
He also declared proudly, "Yeah, I am a communist."

title: Leftist protester disrupts Climate Week event by ranting against US military
summary: Code Pink disrupted a Nature Conservancy event at NYC Climate Week, demanding the group address the Pentagon's carbon footprint and military pollution.
story: Members of the far-left group labeled "U.S. warfare" as one of the greatest threats on Earth. (Credit: CodePink via Storyful)

A member of Code Pink, the far-left group known for confronting elected officials, disrupted a Climate Week event in New York City Thursday, blaming the U.S. military for its perceived role in the climate crisis.

The disruption targeted an event hosted by The Nature Conservancy, which the group claims refuses to address the U.S. military’s "massive carbon footprint and massive environmental degradation from U.S. military bases and U.S.-driven wars and occupations."

"There is an elephant in the room that The Nature Conservancy does not want to address," said a man identified by Code Pink only as Aaron, the campaign organizer for the group's War Is Not Green initiative. "It is destroying ecosystems. It is destroying fish. It is destroying the world."
$54M CODEPINK-LINKED FOUNDATION SHUT DOWN IN CALIFORNIA POPS UP AT RAMSHACKLE MIAMI HOME

Code Pink co-founder Medea Benjamin (left) and activist Tighe Barry protest during the Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing for Defense Secretary nominee Pete Hegseth on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., Jan. 14, 2025. On Thursday, the group protested at The Nature Conservancy in New York City, demanding the group acknowledge the U.S. military's role in the climate crisis. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

He also pointed to the Pentagon’s $1.5 trillion budget and the U.S. military’s role in environmental destruction, asking why The Nature Conservancy, with a budget of over $2 billion and a mission dedicated to protecting land and water, refuses to address it, the group said.

Code Pink said it was present at NYC Climate Week to insist that any serious climate conversation must include the military-industrial complex, which it argued contributes significantly to global warming.
INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE'
CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin holds a poster from a campaign the nonprofit started called China Is Not Our Enemy. (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Code Pink demanded that The Nature Conservancy and other environmental groups "publicly acknowledge the U.S. military as a leading institutional polluter," "refuse partnerships or funding tied to the military-industrial complex" and "use their platforms to demand cuts to the Pentagon budget and an end to wars that devastate ecosystems."

"You cannot claim to protect the land and waters while ignoring the largest institutional polluter on Earth," Aaron explained after the disruption. "The Nature Conservancy has a $2 billion budget and a global platform. It has a responsibility to name the war machine as a driver of climate destruction. Silence is complicity."

title: New Jersey Lt Gov Dale Caldwell resigns after sexual harassment investigation
summary: New Jersey Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell resigned after an investigation substantiated sexual harassment and ethics violations, Gov. Mikie Sherrill announced Friday.
story: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill addresses the resignation of Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell following the release of an ethics report.
Democrat New Jersey Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell resigned Friday after an independent investigation substantiated sexual harassment and ethics violations against him, Gov. Mikie Sherrill announced.

"The investigation found that the lieutenant governor failed to uphold the responsibilities of his office, and he demonstrated a pattern of behavior that does not meet the standards of this administration," Sherrill said during a news conference in Trenton. title: Federal illegal voting arrest becomes latest flashpoint in Sherrill's battles with Trump administration
summary: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill faces new pressure after ICE and the FBI arrested a Senegalese national accused of voting illegally since 2018.
story: Fox News correspondent Eric Shawn reports on the Department of Justice launching an investigation into New Jersey voter roll software errors that registered 6,600 non-citizens to vote. Gov. Mikie Sherrill acknowledged that as many as 400 registered non-citizens cast ballots in state elections under former Gov. Phil Murphy. Department of Homeland Security Sec. Markwayne Mullin warned that up to 35,000 non-citizens may remain registered on New Jersey voter rolls.

Federal law enforcement arrested a Senegalese immigrant in New Jersey accused of illegally voting in multiple elections, injecting a new flashpoint into Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill's escalating fights with Washington over immigration enforcement and election integrity.

The case comes as Washington and Trenton battle over immigration enforcement and election administration, with the Trump administration challenging Sherrill over state policies affecting federal law enforcement while also pressing New Jersey for access to its voter rolls.

Sanata Coulibaly, a Senegalese national, was arrested when DHS and FBI agents jointly executed a criminal warrant in Hudson County, which stretches from West New York to Bayonne across the Hudson River from Manhattan.
FOUR NONCITIZENS CHARGED WITH ILLEGALLY VOTING IN 2020, 2022 AND 2024 FEDERAL ELECTIONS IN NEW JERSEY

"This alien from Senegal has been charged with procurement of citizenship or naturalization unlawfully and voting by an alien after allegedly voting in three general elections in New Jersey," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.
"Sanctuary politicians can try to claim that this kind of voter fraud isn’t happening, but it’s very real and is a serious threat to our country."
WATCH: TRUMP DOJ VOWS TO PURSUE ‘EVERY SINGLE’ VOTING VIOLATION AFTER NJ ROLL SHOCKER

New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill signed Executive Order 12 restricting certain immigration enforcement activities on state property shortly after taking office in January. (Eduardo Munoz Alvarez/Getty Images)
Mullin said DHS and the Trump administration would continue efforts to protect election integrity.

The arrest comes after Sherrill revealed in July that a software error in New Jersey's motor vehicle system had improperly registered roughly 6,600 people who identified themselves as noncitizens. The state later determined that fewer than 400 of those newly registered because of the error had voted.
After that revelation, New Jersey resisted federal demands to turn over voter rolls while pursuing its own investigation.
Fox News Digital reached out to Sherrill for comment.

According to the criminal complaint, Coulibaly cast ballots in the November 2018 midterm election, the July 2020 primary, the November 2020 general election and the 2024 general election while she was not a U.S. citizen.
Coulibaly registered through a paper application submitted to the Hudson County superintendent of elections in Jersey City, falsely certifying that she was a U.S. citizen, the complaint said.
She first came to the U.S. from Senegal on a B-1 nonimmigrant visa in approximately 1993 and later became a lawful permanent resident, according to the Justice Department.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
A DHS agent, left, participates in the arrest of Sanata Coulibaly, right. (DHS Handout)
Prosecutors allege Coulibaly later applied for U.S. citizenship and falsely stated on her N-400 naturalization application that she had never registered to vote or voted in a federal election.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Coulibaly's case is part of a broader federal election-integrity push, with the Justice Department announcing election-related charges against 16 people across several states this month.
Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

title: Reporter's Notebook: Democrats face an impeachment tractor beam that could derail their affordability message
summary: Like the Millenium Falcon caught in a tractor beam, Hakeem Jeffries and House Democrats face an impeachment pull they may not be able to escape.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram previews Congress’ return to Washington and the legislative issues facing lawmakers ahead of the midterms, including artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency regulation.

In the original Star Wars, Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, Chewbacca and Obi-Wan Kenobi find the Millennium Falcon under fire from Imperial TIE fighters in deep outer space. Luke speculates that the TIE fighters are "heading for that small moon."
But Obi-Wan’s visage grows grim.
"That’s no moon," intones Obi-Wan. "It’s a space station."
Han Solo disagrees.
"It’s too big to be a space station," says Han. To which, Obi-Wan instructs him, "Turn the ship around."
But as quickly as he dismissed Kenobi’s observation, Solo pivots. He grimaces, realizing that the wise Jedi Knight is on to something.
DEMOCRAT AL GREEN TO FORCE HOUSE-WIDE VOTE ON IMPEACHING TRUMP

U.S. President Donald Trump takes questions from the media during a bilateral meeting with President of Lebanon Joseph Aoun in the Oval Office of the White House on July 21, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)
"Yeah. I think you’re right," Han replies. The Millennium Falcon starts to shake.
"Chewie, lock in the auxiliary power," Han commands his shipmate. "Why are we still moving towards it?" squeaks Luke.
"We’re caught in a tractor beam and it’s pulling us in!" shouts Han.

And a few moments later, the Millenium Falcon, the fastest ship in the galaxy, is suctioned into Bay 327 of the Death Star, moored, and unable to escape. The band of ragtag heroes are now stuck. On the Death Star.
Grand Moff Tarkin describes it as "the ultimate power in the universe."

Impeachment in Congress is kind of like the Death Star’s tractor beam. You can’t escape once you’re in its clenches. A decision to impeach sucks a political party in, eventually marooning everyone in the political equivalent of a hangar bay.
For Democrats, they can’t focus on the price of eggs and milk. There’s little debate about gas prices. It’s a challenge to even address oversight issues.
You can try to "lock in the auxiliary power." But it’s too late.
You might think impeachment is "a moon." But it’s really the political Death Star.
Not for your adversary. But often those orchestrating the impeachment.

Democrats might find themselves in an impeachment bind if they capture the majority next year. Progressives and the left will possess one of the loudest voices in Congress. And even though Democrats twice impeached President Trump in 2019 and 2021, some will insist on doing it again. That’s to say nothing of trying to impeach a host of Trump Administration cabinet officials – ranging from Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth to Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.
Some Democrats are already falling prey to the impeachment tractor beam.

Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, led the initial effort to impeach President Trump during his first term in 2017 – long before the successful impeachment over Ukraine in 2019. Republican redistricting – engineered by President Trump forced Green out of his Houston-based district earlier this year. But Green engineered yet another effort to impeach the President last week as the Texas Democrat heads for the exit.
MIDTERM HISTORY MASSIVELY FAVORS DEMOCRATS. BUT THEY ARE MAKING A BIG MISTAKE
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) speaks during a press conference on Capitol Hill on November 3, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images)

The House voted to sidestep Green’s impeachment resolution, 232-147. So this was not a straight, up or down vote on impeachment. It was one step removed. Forty-seven Democrats voted "present." That includes the party’s top three Democrats: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., House Minority Whip Katherine Clark (D-MA) and House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif.
In some respects, House Democratic leaders want to shun impeachment. Or at least avoid it for the time being.

In 2006, Democrats were on the precipice of flipping control of the House. Democrats largely won the midterms that year because of voter fatigue with President George W. Bush and the calcification of the war in Iraq.
Many Democrats wanted to impeach the President. But as she prepared to clasp the gavel, then-House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., famously declared that impeachment was "off the table."

House Democrats focused on drawing down the war in Iraq and eventually pivoting to other policy issues like health care and climate change. But Democrats had to get through those midterms first. So once Pelosi said no impeachment, there was no impeachment of the President.

Impeachment with President Trump was kind of "off the table" for Pelosi when Democrats reclaimed the House in the 2018 midterms. But there was a shift among moderate Democrats after disclosures about the President and Ukraine in the summer of 2019. A master of the political pulse, the Speaker understood the direction this was going among her Members. That’s when Pelosi got in front of her caucus, pushing for potential impeachment of the President later that year.

House Democratic leaders are depositing any overt discussion of impeachment on the backburner for now. They don’t want to veer away from their message about affordability. In fact they’ve frequently steered the conversation back to the cost of living when pressed about impeachment.
Consider this response from Jeffries when questioned about impeachment on April 9.

"We'll have a conversation led by (Rep.) Jamie Raskin, D-Md., the top Democrat on the Judiciary Committee, and (Rep.) Jerry Nadler, D-N.Y., a former Judiciary Committee Chairman and Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y., and Judiciary Committee Democrats tomorrow about Trump administration accountability," replied Jeffries.
But, unlike completely mimicking Pelosi’s posture years ago, Jeffries signaled he was open to the impeachment question.
"I don't want to get out ahead of that discussion. But we've also been very clear. House Democrats are going to focus on making life more affordable for the American people," said Jeffries.
On June 14, Kristen Welker of NBC asked Jeffries if his party could "move to impeach President Trump" if Democrats reclaimed the House.

"We haven't ruled anything in or ruled anything out in terms of accountability. What we have said is that our focus is going to be to make life more affordable for the American people," answered Jeffries.
On August 25 on CNN, Jeffries deflected a similar impeachment inquiry.
"We haven't ruled anything in and we haven t ruled anything out," stated Jeffries.
Impeachment interrogatives continued for Jeffries during a September 13 interview on ABC.
"We haven't ruled anything in and we haven't ruled anything out in terms of impeachment," said Jeffries.

That’s smart politics for Jeffries. He’s trying to keep his hand on the helm before the midterms – and essentially deferring to the political climate of next year and where rank-and-file Democrats might fall next year should Democrats capture the majority. But there are indications that many Democrats are already ready for impeachment. The progressive base will demand action. And it extends well beyond Al Green.
Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-Pa., made her case after the President posted to social media in April
that "a whole civilization will die tonight" in reference to Iran.
"If that's not high crimes and misdemeanors - and if it's not madness - I don't know what is," said Dean.
Rep. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., said that the President was "threatening genocide."
Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said the party should "push for impeachment" and that the President "is unfit to be the Commander in Chief" and "should be removed."

So Jeffries has a decision to make. The hard left will demand impeachment – for someone. Be it the President or Hegseth. But if Democrats flip the House, their "majority makers" might represent battleground districts. Those prospective lawmakers will be moderates. Impeachment could be politically toxic for them.
TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS

Rep. Al Green speaks during a news conference outside the U.S. Capitol on July 23, 2025, in Washington, DC. Rep. Green held a news conference to discuss impeaching President Donald Trump. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

Pelosi’s circumstances evolved in the summer of 2019. Moderate Democrats with national security credentials from swing districts edged toward impeachment. So, she pulled the impeachment trigger. Pelosi knew the direction of her caucus.
In September 2026, it’s not as clear for Jeffries. And it’s not a done deal that Democrats will seize the majority.
That’s why the New York Democrat expressed caution during his conversation on ABC.
"We've got to follow the facts. Apply the law. Be guided by the Constitution and then let the chips fall where they may, in the best interest of the American people," said Jeffries.
Han Solo was skeptical back on the Death Star.
"Even if I could take off, I’d never get past the tractor beam," said Solo.
"Leave that to me," promised Obi-Wan Kenobi.
The Jedi Master then eluded detection on the Death Star, manually shutting off the tractor beam. That disgorged the Millenium Falcon. But in the end, Kenobi sacrificed himself for the mission.
On Capitol Hill, impeachment is a tractor beam. Once you’re siphoned in, nothing can escape its grasp. Debates about policy. Spending. Health care. War. The tractor beam controls all.
Until it’s switched off.
Not every party which is incapacitated by impeachment has an Obi-Wan Kenobi who can find the off switch. When it comes to impeachment best advice might be to "turn the ship around" beforehand.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
But if lots of Members are clamoring for impeachment, it may already be too late.
Chad Pergram currently serves as Chief Congressional Correspondent for FOX News Channel (FNC). He joined the network in September 2007 and is based out of Washington, D.C.

title: Xi praises US state visit 'perfection' as Trump calls meetings 'very productive'
summary: President Donald Trump said Friday that the U.S. and China have "made great strides" after meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House.
story: President Donald Trump said Friday that the two world leaders had a "very productive" time this week in Washington, D.C.

Chinese President Xi Jinping praised the level of "perfection" on display during his state visit to the White House, and President Donald Trump said Friday the two world leaders had a "very productive" time in Washington.

Trump, speaking to reporters as he and first lady Melania Trump hosted Xi and first lady of China Madame Peng Liyuan for tea at the White House, said, "We've had a tremendous visit from two spectacular people," and, "we've made great strides, very positive for both countries."

"I want to thank the honorable president and the first lady for everything they've done for myself and my wife during this visit. Everything is down to the highest order of perfection," Xi responded through a translator. "And there is thought in every little detail. And it's greatly appreciated.
XI CAPS TRUMP STATE VISIT WITH SYMBOLIC FINAL STOP BEFORE LEAVING WASHINGTON

"The president and I are like two people that's charting the course for the great ship of China-U.S. relations," he continued. "When the president visited China in May, we agreed on the vision of building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability.

"This time, we've agreed to add new substance to it. That's the relationship, will be a constructive one of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity. So, from this, one can see that the prospects for this relationship will get more brighter."

President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump attend a tea with China's President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, in the Red Room of the White House Friday, Sept. 25, 2026, in Washington. (Jacquelyn Martin/AP)

Xi, the leader of China’s ruling Communist Party, said he had two more opportunities to meet Trump this year, first at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in China in November and then at the G20 Summit in December at Trump’s Doral resort in Miami, Florida.

"We will see you, and we'll be speaking a lot. I think our farmers are going to be very happy," Trump said Friday. "A lot of very positive things happened. But America is very happy about this visit, and I'm sure China is very happy also. Great things for both countries. And it's been just very, very productive."
TRUMP-XI REUNION COMES WITH UNFINISHED BUSINESS — AND A BIGGER BATTLE LOOMING

First lady of China Peng Liyuan and President Xi Jinping sit with President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump in the Oval Office at the White House on Sept. 24, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Xi arrived in Washington Wednesday evening for a summit with Trump, four months after the two leaders reached a sweeping agreement that included Chinese commitments on rare earths, agricultural purchases, trade and investment.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump greet Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, at the National Archives Museum Friday, Sept. 25, 2026, in Washington. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP)

Trump hailed that agreement as a breakthrough for American farmers, manufacturers and workers. But the latest talks unfolded during uneven progress on commitments involving rare-earth minerals, agricultural and commercial purchases, trade and investment, while key disputes over tariffs, advanced technology, artificial intelligence, intellectual property and Taiwan remain unresolved.

"President Xi and Madam Peng have just left D.C., heading for China. The meeting was one of Friendship, Strength, and Success, for both China and the U.S.A.," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Much has been, and will be, accomplished. I look forward to our next meeting!"
Fox News Digital’s Ashley J. DiMella and Peter D’Abrosca contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: 'Squad' Democrat slammed by Trump admin for most 'radical' plan targeting ICE yet
summary: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin fires back at Rep. Delia Ramirez's radical bill to abolish ICE, CBP, and dismantle the Department of Homeland Security.
story: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin joins 'Saturday in America' to highlight border enforcement updates and criticize the Biden administration border policies following 16 straight months of zero releases under current enforcement. He reiterates that DHS and ICE remain committed to targeting high-risk individuals to keep American communities safe.
EXCLUSIVE: Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin is firing back at a progressive House Democrat who is pushing one of the most radical Trump administration crackdowns yet.

Mullin and his DHS spokesperson both criticized legislation by Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., a member of the progressive "Squad," that would dismantle most of the department and abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

"Radical leftists are calling to defund the police and abolish DHS. It’s NEVER going to happen. Our 270,000 DHS patriots are keeping Americans SAFE— unlike this open-borders politician who refuses to prioritize Americans over illegal aliens," Mullin told Fox News Digital.
DHS CHIEF FIRES BACK AT JAYAPAL OVER CLAIM MAJORITY OF IMMIGRATION ARRESTS POSE 'NO THREAT'

Rep. Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., is pushing a new bill to abolish ICE and Customs and Border Protection while dismantling DHS in its current state. (Jemal Countess/Getty Images for The Service Employees International Union (SEIU); Pat Greenhouse/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

His spokesperson went even further, telling Fox News Digital that Ramirez "should be thanking our law enforcement for removing these dangerous criminals from her district—NOT vilifying law enforcement."

"This type of rhetoric is contributing to a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them as they put their lives on the line," the DHS spokesperson said. "While sanctuary politicians smear ICE, law enforcement is arresting criminals and saving countless American lives."
DEMS SHAMED AS DHS BRINGS ICE SHOOTING RECEIPTS AFTER POLITICIAN CALLED ICE OFFICERS ‘LIARS WITH MASKS’

DHS also pointed Fox News Digital to a list of illegal immigrants arrested in Ramirez's home state of Illinois. It included Bulgarian national Rumen Georgriev, who was convicted of "rape with a weapon," Abdukadir Haji of Somalia, who DHS said was convicted of "sex assault and rape," and Cuban national Samuel Reyes-Silva, who was convicted of "robbery and homicide."
Ramirez's legislation, the Reimagining Safety Act, would create a "Department of Community Safety" while dismantling DHS as it is currently known.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin speaks during a news conference at the Eisenhower Executive Office Building on July 17, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Jim Lo Scalzo/EPA/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Certain agencies like the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Coast Guard, and customs functions would be preserved.

The bill would abolish ICE and "begin the process of establishing a separate civil immigration system," according to a release. It would also abolish Customs and Border Protection (CBP), the agency charged with keeping the southern border free of illegal crossings.
TLAIB MOVES TO BLOCK ICE AIRPORT ARRESTS, SAYS TSA HELPING TARGET IMMIGRANTS

Democrat calls to abolish ICE have swelled in recent months amid bipartisan criticism of President Donald Trump's handling of immigration, reigniting most recently when agents shot a Venezuelan national in Austin, Texas. Backlash has also been targeted at federal immigration officials' killing of two U.S. citizens earlier this year.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents walk a detainee out of the Ventura County Government Center in Ventura, Calif., on July 27, 2026. (Blake Fagan/AFP via Getty Images)
But Ramirez's bill would go further in dismantling the current anti-illegal immigration enforcement system with its call to end CBP as well as ICE.

She fired back at the Trump administration's criticism in a statement to Fox News Digital, "Every day, Americans wake up with a new reason to dismantle DHS, reimagine safety, and build something that honors our shared humanity. The people have the power to reshape the government: instead of the weapon DHS has proven to be, we need a department built on the best parts of who we are and can be, and the best examples of how we can take care of each other in hard times."

"Markwayne and DHS will keep spreading cheap lies and fearmongering in a desperate attempt to save face because dismantling DHS and building something new is part of how we hold them accountable, stop corruption, and end their lawlessness," Ramirez said.
