The governor said her demand that Caldwell step down is part of her efforts to dismantle a culture that ignores victims.

“There has been a culture in Trenton, probably since the birth of our nation, to sweep this under the rug,” Sherrill said. “That is not the kind of government I’m running. When I say there is a culture change taking place, I mean it. This is part of it.”
New Jersey state Assembly Speaker Craig Coughlin, a Democrat, applauded Sherrill for her “commitment to hold public officials to the highest standards.”

“Following an independent investigation, Lieutenant Governor Dale Caldwell was right to resign from office today,” Coughlin said in a statement. “We must ensure the work of governing is uninterrupted and that serving the people of New Jersey remains a top priority.”
Caldwell was also serving as New Jersey’s secretary of state, an office that oversees elections.
Sherrill said Friday that the state’s acting comptroller, Shirley Emehelu, would become acting secretary of state with just weeks to go until the midterm elections.

“Shirley is a veteran of the U.S. Department of Justice and the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office,” Sherrill said. “She has the judgment to run these elections and the strength to stand up to Trump’s attacks on voting.”

The lieutenant governor’s duties also include filling in for the governor when she leaves the state. Sherrill said that until a new lieutenant governor is in place, there is “an order of command” for who would step in for her during any absence, beginning with the state Senate president.

Under New Jersey law, the lieutenant governor must be replaced within 45 days of the position becoming vacant. Sherrill said she would “certainly” make a permanent appointment within that time frame but does not plan on naming an acting lieutenant governor in the meantime.

“We will be making sure with our chief counsel that we’re following the rules,” Sherrill said. “This is a little bit of a new area for New Jersey, so we’re going to ensure that we get legal opinions and follow the process there.”

title: Police believe Tasia Fortune’s hanging was staged as new details revealed in court
summary: JACKSON, Miss. — Authorities believe Tasia Fortune’s hanging was staged and that she was possibly killed at another location before being found behind an abandoned Mississippi home, a detective said in court Friday.
story: JACKSON, Miss. — Authorities believe Tasia Fortune’s hanging was staged and that she was possibly killed at another location before being found behind an abandoned Mississippi home, a detective said in court Friday.
New details about Fortune’s death last month were revealed during a court hearing for Jarques Ratliff, one of the two men arrested and charged with murder.
At a court hearing earlier this month, Ratliff, 51, was denied bond after he pleaded not guilty.
Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman, was found hanging from a tree behind the Jackson home on Aug. 3. Officials believe she may have been dead for two or three days before she was found.
A motive in the killing and a cause of death have not been released.

A detective said at Friday’s hearing that there may have been an issue over missing illegal narcotics. The detective declined to release additional details because the grand jury has not received all of the evidence.
Ratliff, 51, told the court that Fortune was his friend.
His attorney, Toney Baldwin, said he wants the “truth about what happened to come out.”
“My client said he’s not involved and that’s absolutely what I believe,” he said.
Fortune’s mother, Christy Spivey, said she wants to know what evidence police have.
The other man arrested and charged in Fortune’s death is Earnest Lloyd Jr. Police have also obtained a warrant for a third suspect. Both Lloyd and Ratliff are Black.

Lloyd, 25, allegedly had a physical altercation with Fortune either days or minutes before she died, NBC affiliate WLBT of Jackson reported. He was accused of hanging Fortune with a black cable cord, according to the news station.
Bracey Harris reported from Jackson, Mississippi, and Minyvonne Burke reported from Pittsburgh.

title: Jay-Z accuser says her rape claims against him were false
summary: The woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has recanted her allegations against the music mogul.
story: The woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has recanted her allegations against the music mogul.

In a filing Thursday from lawyers representing Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, the former accuser says that her allegations against the rapper were “false,” adding that she “never met Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever. There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr. Carter.”
In the filing, she added that she falsely claimed that Carter and Sean “Diddy” Combs raped her while watched by another celebrity, whose name is redacted.

The filing is part of Carter’s ongoing malicious prosecution lawsuit against the woman’s former attorney, Tony Buzbee, which was filed in February 2025 in New York. Carter’s lawyers said this week they were dropping the woman, known as Jane Doe, from the suit.

Buzbee, Jane Doe, and representatives for Carter and Combs didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. Combs is serving a sentence in federal prison after he was convicted in July 2025 of prostitution-related crimes, in a separate case.

The woman came forward in December 2024, in a civil lawsuit filed by Buzbee, accusing Carter and Combs of raping her at a house party following the 2000 MTV Video Music Awards, which were held in New York. Days after the suit was filed, she sat down with NBC News for an interview and doubled down on her claims. But after NBC News pointed out inconsistencies in her account, she said in a subsequent phone interview that she had “made some mistakes.”
At the time, Combs’ attorneys described the suit as a “shameful money grab” while Carter’s lawyer Alex Spiro called it a “frivolous case.”
In February 2025, Jane Doe dropped her lawsuit with prejudice, meaning she couldn’t file it again.

In this week’s filing, Jane Doe writes: “I understand that my false accusations have caused Mr. Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone. I sincerely and unconditionally apologize to Mr. Carter for the devastating harm I have caused to him, his family and his reputation.”
She also says in the filing that Buzbee and his team paid her $1,000 before sitting down for NBC News’ interview.

In a separate suit, Jay-Z initially sued Buzbee in 2024 in California, accusing Buzbee of extortion and defamation. It was dismissed in June 2025, and the California Court of Appeals affirmed that decision earlier this month. Representatives for Buzbee and his law firm called the appeals court’s ruling “a complete vindication for our clients.”

title: Mississippi police seize kratom and make arrests after deaths of Ole Miss students
summary: Two people were arrested and a load of kratom seized, Mississippi authorities said Friday, days following the mysterious deaths of two Ole Miss students who were found with kratom at the scene.
story: Two people were arrested and a load of kratom seized, Mississippi authorities said Friday, days following the mysterious deaths of two Ole Miss students who were found with kratom at the scene.
Metro Narcotics agents on Thursday raided the Puffs Vape, Tobacco and Beer Store, located in the 100 block of Heritage Drive in Oxford, officials said.
Agents seized “more than 500 units of kratom, along with an assortment of THC cartridges, gummies, and other suspected narcotics,” according to am Oxford police statement,.
The possession, distribution and sale of kratom has been prohibited from Oxford in 2019, police said.

Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Mohamed, 18, were booked for various drug offenses. The store’s owner, 40-year-old Amer Alowdi, was indicted for allegedly trafficking narcotics in 2022, officials said.
He fled the country before prosecution and “additional charges may be forthcoming as the investigation continues” in this matter, officials said.

Aidan Hamilton, 18, a freshman from Englewood, Colorado, and Robert Strang, 20, a junior from Atlanta, were found dead in separate locations this week, Ole Miss said. Their causes of death have not been announced and it is not clear if kratom played any role.
Their deaths sparked renewed concerns about the drug, which officials said was found at the scene of both deaths.

Kratom is an herb with opioidlike effects. It has gained popularity in the U.S. as an unapproved treatment for pain, anxiety and drug dependence. Kratom can be stimulating or sedating, depending on the dosage taken, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration.
It wasn’t immediately clear on Friday if these arrests have any connection to the Hamilton and Strang deaths.
This is a developing story, Please check back here for updates.

title: James Comey seashells case delayed until early 2027
summary: The seashells-based prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey has been delayed until early 2027, as a judge makes her way through a number of pending motions, including a request by Comey to dismiss the case on grounds that it was driven by President Donald Trump’s animus.
story: The seashells-based prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey has been delayed until early 2027, as a judge makes her way through a number of pending motions, including a request by Comey to dismiss the case on grounds that it was driven by President Donald Trump’s animus.

U.S. District Judge Louise Flanagan declined to set a trial date in the case against Comey, in which prosecutors say that a photo he posted on Instagram of seashells arranged to spell out “8647” amounted to a threat against the president. The term “86” is widely considered to be restaurant slang for running out of or canceling an item, and 47 is thought to be a reference to the 47th president.
Comey, who has not entered a plea yet in the case, had been set to be arraigned Wednesday at a federal courthouse in New Bern, North Carolina, but Flanagan pushed the arraignment until January.
Comey’s team had asked to delay the case.
“The gravity of the charges, pending motions, and the need to provide defense counsel additional time to prepare for trial promote need for continuance,” Flanagan wrote in an order Friday.

Comey’s extensive legal team has filed numerous motions to dismiss the case, which has come under intense scrutiny from legal experts. Comey’s team contended the prosecution was “not based on a good-faith application of the law to the facts; instead, it effectuates a yearslong campaign by the President to use the criminal process to punish Mr. Comey for his protected speech and because of the President’s deep-seated animosity.”
Comey’s team also spotlighted what it calls the “extreme bias” of a key witness in the seashells case: an estranged associate of the Comeys who said they hoped Comey went to jail.
The lead prosecutor in the case, a rookie federal prosecutor named Matthew Petracca, left the prosecution in May.

title: Man arrested six years after his wife’s remains were found in a crawlspace
summary: A man in Southern California is facing murder charges in connection to his wife’s killing 20 years ago.
story: A man in Southern California is facing murder charges in connection to his wife’s killing 20 years ago.
Jeff Anthony Maiorca, 53, was arrested Monday after local authorities in San Bernardino discovered the remains of Jill Maiorca hidden in the crawlspace beneath a home in Big Bear.
Jill Maiorca was reported missing from Big Bear Lake in 2007 and authorities now say she was murdered in November 2006, according to the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department. She was 29.

Authorities resumed their investigation into her disappearance on Oct. 28, 2020, when deputies from the Big Bear Sheriff’s Station responded to a call from someone who reported “a suspicious discovery in the crawlspace” under a residence, the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department said in a news release on Monday night. Upon arrival, they realize that hidden beneath the home were “unidentified human remains.”
An autopsy conducted on the remains determined the manner of death to be homicide.

In 2023, the remains were identified as those of Jill Maiorca following “additional investigative DNA analysis” after cold case homicide investigators took over the case, according to the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department. Her remains had long been concealed beneath the Big Bear house without the homeowner’s knowledge.
Cold case detectives eventually identified Jill Maiorca’s former husband, Jeff Maiorca, as a suspect in her murder.
Public records show Jeff Maiorca had filed for divorce from Jill Maiorca in Los Angeles County in 2004.

Local authorities detained Jeff Maiorca on Monday afternoon at the Big Bear Lake branch library on Garstin Drive, arrest records show. He is currently being held without bail at the High Desert Jail in Adelanto, California.

Records from the San Bernardino County Superior Court in California show Jeff Maiorca had an initial hearing on Wednesday. He was formally charged with murder and use of a deadly weapon, records show.
Records do not yet list an attorney for Jeff Maiorca. His next court hearing is scheduled for Oct. 12.

The investigation into Jill Maiorca’s disappearance and death remain ongoing. The San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department is encouraging anyone with information to contact their homicide detail team.

title: Should you bring iced coffee to a job interview? Question brews generational debate
summary: What started as a conversation about job interview tips online escalated into a generational debate over whether it’s taboo to show up with an iced coffee to talk to a potential employer.
story: What started as a conversation about job interview tips online escalated into a generational debate over whether it’s taboo to show up with an iced coffee to talk to a potential employer.

The discourse over the caffeinated beverage gained momentum on TikTok this week after a creator, who goes by @caitlinrecruiter on the platform, shared a video in which she said she believes “when you show up with an iced coffee or an iced latte that this interview is just a stop on your list of errands for the day.”
“It looks a little too casual to me,” she said in the video, which she posted Sept. 16.

Caitlin Wehniainen, whose profile states she has 16 years of recruiting experience, has just over 1,000 followers on TikTok. But in the last week, her video has been clipped and recirculated by dozens of creators online, who engaged in a heated back-and-forth about whether she’s right.
The divide seemed to primarily be between younger and older users — with the former group suggesting Wehniainen’s tip “makes no sense at all” and that such a perspective is archaic.

Others, many who identified as Gen Xers in comments, agreed with Wehniainen, writing that “arguing against this is insane” and telling applicants that they should “save the iced coffee for when you actually get hired.”

By Monday, even the coffee giant Starbucks had taken a side, alluding to the debate in an Instagram post that featured an image of someone holding an iced coffee in one hand and sunglasses and their handbag in the other. “Pulling up to the interview like,” the caption read. Meanwhile, The Coffee Bean and Tea Leaf, another coffee chain, commented on Wehniainen’s video: “We’d hire them on spot...”
When reached for comment on Friday, Wehniainen said in an email to NBC News that she was “shocked at how polarizing the topic is.”

“But I realize that the original message was taken out of context as the virality of the post grew,” she wrote. “As the topic spread, many decided to weigh in with their own general opinion on whether or not bringing an iced coffee into an interview is appropriate ... I also saw people reading into it too much, asking if coffee or water matters and what is appropriate. I will say, I think a bottled water is great to bring with you.”

The timing of the conversation coincides with a tough job market: Recent college graduates are facing higher unemployment rates than other age groups as it’s becoming more difficult to obtain entry-level jobs, NBC News reported last month. Employers are not looking to add talent, and employed people are not moving to new positions, as a rise in AI continues to threaten jobs.

For Los Angeles-based TikTok creator Esha, who preferred to be identified by only her first name, citing privacy concerns, Wehniainen’s words couldn’t be further from the truth. She was among the many weighing in online, telling her 81,000-plus TikTok followers that “the iced coffee controversy completely misunderstands interviews.”

“Thinking of a job interview as a stop in your day is very normal,” Esha, 22, added in an interview with NBC News, noting that she’s brought iced coffees to several interviews and hasn’t thought twice about it.
“Gen Z had this shift in recent years, where we can still have a life outside of work,” Esha said. “So, like, why am I changing who I am? Why am I missing my coffee for the day for this interview?”
In her video, she elaborated further on her take, saying that “the most easily relatable thing in corporate America is a coffee addiction.”

“Unless you’re like over the age of 30 and you can relate on having kids, and doing stuff with your kids, coffee is the main thing. Everyone’s like, ‘Gotta get that coffee’ ... and finding something personable about a person is so important,” she said. “Like, who is not starting their workday off with a coffee?”
Catherine Fisher, vice president of communications at LinkedIn, said she’s not surprised by the generational divisions when it comes to job etiquette.

“Gen Z is entering this workforce at such a challenging time, it’s such a competitive job market, and to then get judged by bringing an iced coffee just seems like, ‘Have we lost the plot here?’” she said.
That said, Fisher is among the cohort who believes it’s best to skip the iced coffee when headed to an interview.

“Even though I don’t like the answer, I think because everyone is so divided on it, I would be cautious and not bring one,” she said. “You just don’t know who’s on the other side of the interview, so why risk it over something so silly?”
Etiquette expert Thomas Farley, who is known as Mister Manners to his followers online, agreed with the more traditional point of view.

“I think it sends the wrong message in so many respects,” he said. “I think it shows you to be someone who didn’t plan your time accordingly, and you’re multitasking, and that’s not what you should be doing during the interview.”
Farley also warned of the physical pratfalls a coffee could bring.
“There are real practical considerations when you bring a liquid into someone’s office,” he said. “Where does it go? What happens if you spill it?”
While he doesn’t think it should be the deciding factor for any hiring manager, Farley argued candidates should be doing everything in their power to leave a positive impression.

“If it’s between you and three other people, and everyone’s qualifications are more or less equal, and that’s the one thing that potentially sinks your chance to get the job, I think that would be really unfortunate,” he said. “That would be a very expensive $7 cup of iced coffee.”
Still, Gen Zers like Esha are not convinced that bringing the beverage would make or break their job opportunity.
As another TikTok creator put it in their video: “It’s really, really not that serious most of the time.”
As for Wehniainen? Even after the online uproar, she said her “opinion still stands that you shouldn’t bring an iced coffee to your interview.”
“You want to leave outlying distractions like iced coffee behind,” she said, “and connect with your interviewer with full attention.”

title: Ed Sheeran shows at Gillette Stadium are canceled due to weather
summary: Ed Sheeran’s concerts scheduled for this weekend at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts have been canceled due to a nor’easter, amid wider turmoil surrounding the British pop star’s tour.
story: Ed Sheeran’s concerts scheduled for this weekend at Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts have been canceled due to severe weather, amid wider turmoil surrounding the British pop star’s tour.

The concerts scheduled for Friday and Saturday at the New England Patriots home stadium were scrapped because of the upcoming nor’easter, Messina Touring, Sheeran’s touring group, said in an Instagram statement.

“Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium,” the statement said. “The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority.”
The touring group said that refunds are available and that ticket holders who purchased through Ticketmaster will be automatically refunded.
The announcement comes amid a wider scandal for Sheeran’s “Loop” tour since one of its opening acts was forced out for voicing pro-Palestinian views.

Earlier this month, rapper Macklemore said he was removed from Sheeran’s tour after speaking out in support for the Palestinian people at the tour’s shows in New Jersey. Macklemore said he was removed at the behest of New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft and alleged that Kraft organized a boycott among stadium owners.
Kraft did not immediately return a request for comment. In a previous statement he said he did not intend to stifle Palestinian support but to ensure a “welcoming environment” at Gillette Stadium.
Macklemore’s removal prompted Sheeran’s other opening acts — Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham, Finneas and his house band, Beoga — to withdraw in protest.
A rep for Sheeran did not immediately return a request for comment. In his first concert since the scandal, Sheeran apologized for the scenario.

“I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician,” Sheeran said, “but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet.”
On Thursday, Macklemore announced a Free Palestine Tour for this fall.

The multiday nor’easter is expected to hit the East Coast, affecting states from Virginia to Rhode Island. Coastal flood alerts are in effect for 33 million people. Wind gusts are expected to peak on Saturday, reaching up to 60 mph in coastal locations.

Sheeran’s shows weren’t the only major musical events canceled due to the threat of severe weather in the North East, with the Global Citizen Festival at Central Park in New York City also pulling the plug.

“Due to the extreme weather forecast for New York City this weekend, we have made the difficult decision, in consultation with the City of New York and NYC Parks, to cancel this year’s Global Citizen Festival,” the organization wrote on social media.
“Safety has to come first,” Global Citizen added, noting that this is the first time the festival has been canceled in 14 years.
All Things Go, another New York City festival that was to be held at Forrest Hills Stadium in Queens this weekend, was also canceled due to the weather.
And a Friday night concert at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey by Australian rock legends AC/DC was postponed just hours before the show.

title: Mystery solved? Two arrested in connection with NYC’s sewer emergence
summary: Two men were arrested in connection with this week’s mysterious sighting of sewer invaders emerging from a New York City manhole cover, court records revealed on Friday.
story: Two men were arrested in connection with this week’s mysterious sighting of sewer invaders emerging from a New York City manhole cover, court records revealed on Friday.
Samuel Reveron, 25, and Kevin Rodriguez, 26, were each booked on two counts of trespassing.

The pair were implicated in the latest sewer incident, in which men were seen climbing out from underground near East 61st Street and Park Avenue at about 1:38 a.m. Wednesday, according to a criminal complaint.

At around 4 a.m., “the individuals were observed getting back into the vehicles and driving in tandem over the Queensboro Bridge, alerting the automatic license plate readers as to the vehicle’s’ VIN and license plate numbers,” the complaint said.
Reveron and Rodriguez, who own the vehicles, both “identified themselves as the individuals that entered the manhole” early Wednesday morning, according to the court document.
They “both described in sum and substance that they entered the manhole together to look for valuables that get washed away in the storm drains and sewers,” authorities said.
Reveron and Rodriguez have not been charged in other sewer break-ins, but the NYPD said earlier that Wednesday’s incident “fits that same criteria” previous cases of unauthorized sewer entries.
This particular incident raised concerns of local law enforcement, already under strain with the United Nations General Assembly in session and world leaders strolling around New York City.
The 61st and Park sighting came steps away from a hotel where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had stayed in previous New York City visits — though he ultimately did not bunk here this week.
Brian Kennedy, an attorney for Reveron, contested allegations his client was in sewers — but said that if his client were underground, there was no intent to injure anyone.

“It seems like not much of a case,” Kennedy told NBC News on Friday. “I understand that it is strange that it’s alleged he went (into the sewer). But there’s no connection to the UN or the appearance of Netanyahu or any other kind of nefarious scheme.”
Rodriquez’s attorney declined comment.
If it’s proven that Reveron did go underground, Kennedy said he’d counsel his client not to do that again.
“It’s not advised to go into a sewer,” Kennedy said. “Besides the grime and rats, there are other dangers down there. It’s not something I would be doing.”
Earlier this year, there were at least two incidents of men captured on video mysteriously emerging from New York City sewers.
The underground visitors, not affiliated with any public works crews, were seen climbing out of manholes in various Brooklyn neighborhoods in late May.
The incidents reignited New York fascination with the urban lore of “mole men” — mythical Big Apple residents who allegedly reside under city streets.

The myth was fed a dose of reality in 1993 when late journalist Jennifer Toth published “The Mole People: Life in the Tunnels Beneath New York City,” chronicling homeless people living in or around city train tunnels.

title: Frat leaders arrested after pledges found in basement, injured and covered in condiments
summary: Two leaders of an underground University of Wisconsin-Madison fraternity were arrested and charged with hazing after dozens of pledges were found injured, shirtless and covered in condiments in a sweltering basement.
story: Two leaders of an underground University of Wisconsin-Madison fraternity were arrested and charged with hazing after dozens of pledges were found injured, shirtless and covered in condiments in a sweltering basement.
The Madison Police Department said Thursday it received an anonymous tip about an event in the basement of an off-campus chapter house.
Alpha Epsilon Pi was kicked off campus as a recognized chapter in 2015, but the organization maintained a presence at the Madison home.
Police say about 30 pledges, most of whom were 18, were found partially-clothed in a filthy basement around 8:20 p.m. on Wednesday.

The apparent hazing victims were “covered in food, condiments, and other liquids” and “had visible injuries consistent with being physically assaulted.” The thermostat was set to 81 degrees, making the basement hot and humid, police said.
Brayden Klein and Samuel Vane, both 20, were charged with hazing and disorderly conduct. Madison police are still investigating the matter.

Klein and Vane each posted $400 bail around 1 a.m. on Thursday morning and were released from the Dane County Jail, officials confirmed. It was not immediately clear when they must appear in court to face the charges.
Klein and Vane could not immediately be reached by NBC News for comment.

The university said in a statement that while it stopped recognizing Alpha Epsilon Pi about a decade ago, the national organization has continued to recognize the Madison chapter, allowing it to exist in the community.
The University of Wisconsin-Madison said in a statement that it will investigate students “implicated in the incident.”
Alpha Epsilon Pi was founded as a Jewish fraternity in 1913.
The national organization’s website lists a Madison, Wisconsin, chapter called “Pi,” but it does not cite an affiliation with the university.
In a statement, the national fraternity said it is taking the allegations “extremely seriously” and said it would “cooperate fully with the authorities investigating this matter.”

“Any member found responsible for criminal conduct in this matter will be expelled from AEPi, and we will support prosecution to the fullest extent of the law,” the statement said. “We will also work with the university in hopes that they will take action against individual perpetrators for violation of the student code of conduct.”
“Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for ... Anyone who engages in hazing forfeits the privilege of being an AEPi brother,” the statement continued.
Anti-hazing advocates say underground chapters present a unique risk for hazing incidents because they are not monitored by officials at their college or university.
There have been almost 130 hazing-related deaths with an average of five per year in the U.S. since 2000, according to HazingInfo.org, a research and advocacy website that tracks incidents.

title: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to use expanded database for potential voter purges
summary: The Supreme Court permitted the Trump administration to expand a federal database containing citizenship information, as it encourages states to purge people from voter rolls.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Friday permitted the Trump administration to use an expanded federal database containing citizenship information, as the president encourages states to purge people from voter rolls.

The justices, divided 6-3 on ideological lines with conservatives in the majority, granted an emergency request filed by the government after lower courts ruled that the Trump administration’s changes to the database were likely unlawful.
Critics have said the data is unreliable and could lead to U.S. citizens being kicked off the voter rolls.

But the court noted in its unsigned ruling that the National Voter Registration Act bars the broad purging of voter rolls in the weeks leading up to an election, which “limits the potential impact” of the decision this year. States can still make individualized queries about voters.
Add to Google
Add to Google
On the broader legal questions raised in the case, the court said that federal law requires the government to respond to requests from states for information about citizenship.
The lower court injunction “prevents the federal government from using the program it believes is best suited to the task,” the court said.
In dissent, liberal Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson wrote that the government had not done enough to show that the lower court ruling needed to be blocked.

In her view, “the harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the Government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take,” she added.
Various groups challenging the plan, led by the League of Women Voters, have argued that it violates several laws, including the Social Security Act and the Privacy Act.
The Supreme Court decision “puts millions of Americans at risk for being unlawfully targeted by the administration’s unreliable voter purge database,” the groups said in a statement.
Conservative who have backed the administration’s efforts to tighten voting laws, welcomed the decision.
The ruling “just makes it easier for states to get federal citizenship data to help them clean up voter rolls,” Jason Snead, executive director of the Honest Elections Project, said in a statement.

The Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements program, known as SAVE, was set up by Congress in 1986 so that government agencies could quickly determine someone’s immigration status when they applied for benefits like Social Security.

The Trump administration expanded SAVE after President Donald Trump issued an executive order in March 2025 that required agencies to take steps to better ensure that only U.S. citizens vote in elections.
The government expanded the database by adding information from the Social Security Administration, which enabled searches using Social Security numbers and allowed officials to do bulk searches.

After states started putting their voter rolls through the newly expanded system, some local officials noticed mistakes; many of the flagged registrants were newly naturalized citizens, according to reporting from ProPublica and The Texas Tribune.

Texas was one of the first states to put its full voter rolls — more than 18 million registrations — through the SAVE database last year. Just three people have been charged with voting illegally as a noncitizen.
A federal judge blocked the Trump administration plan, with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit reaching the same conclusion.

In court papers, Solicitor General D. John Sauer said that the district court’s ruling “threatens the integrity of upcoming elections” by preventing the government from responding to state requests to verify the citizenship of potential voters.
Opponents argue the expanded database could force bureaucratic obligations on newly naturalized citizens who are asked to prove their citizenship after being flagged by the system.

Noncitizen voting is extremely rare. All states are required to conduct voter roll list maintenance under federal law, and states already have processes to identify any noncitizens who do accidentally make it onto the voter rolls.

title: This is how often you should be cleaning your makeup brushes, according to experts
summary: Dirty makeup brushes can cause breakouts and irritation. Experts share how often to clean your brushes and sponges, plus the best cleaners to get the job done.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans.

Makeup brushes do a lot of work — namely sweeping foundation, blush, powder and other cosmetics onto your face day after day — yet many people rarely think about cleaning them. It’s an easy chore to put off, especially since freshly washed brushes can take up to 24 hours to dry. The only problem with that is that skipping regular cleanings can affect both how your makeup looks and the health of your skin.

“[Not cleaning makeup brushes] can lead to makeup buildup on the brush hairs, which can negatively affect the softness of the bristles over time and lead to a patchy or streaky application,” says Eric Vosburg, a New York City-based makeup artist. “And due to the high moisture content from liquid and cream products, bacteria can easily form and grow, which can cause the contaminated tools to spread bacteria around the skin, leading to acne.”

So, how often should you actually be washing them? I posed that very question to Vosburg and other professional makeup artists and got tips on the best way to actually wash them and recommendations on tools that can help you get the job done.
How often should you clean your makeup brushes?

How often you should wash your makeup brushes depends on how frequently you use them and what you use them for. As a general rule, Vosburg recommends cleaning them once a week to reduce product buildup and keep bristles in good condition. Brushes used with liquid or cream formulas, like foundation and concealer, tend to collect residue and moisture faster than those used with powders, so they need attention more frequently — you may be able to stretch wash time on powder brushes to every two weeks.

Certain situations also call for extra cleanings. If you’ve recently been sick, wash your brushes once you’ve recovered to avoid transferring germs back onto your skin or into your makeup products. And if you’re dealing with acne or breakouts, more frequent cleaning can help limit the spread of bacteria and fungus and prevent reinfection, says Zac Hart, a New York City-based hair and makeup artist.

Between deep cleanings, a quick-dry brush cleaner can be a convenient option, since it removes residue and sanitizes bristles without the long drying time. However, relying on these sprays too often can damage brushes over time and they can leave behind a residue of their own, says Hart. In other words, use them sparingly and only when you absolutely need a quick clean until you’re able to do a thorough one.
The best products to clean makeup brushes

To help you get your makeup brushes as clean as possible, I asked Vosburg and Hart what types of products can be helpful. I then sourced highly-rated options within the categories they recommended. All of the products below have at least a four-star average rating from more than a thousand shoppers.

It’s gross and fascinating at the same time,” she says. “I love that I don’t have to do a bunch of scrubbing like I do with bar soaps and the residue comes off when I rinse it under the faucet. The gnarly smell is definitely the one drawback, but it’s nothing one pump of hand soap can’t take away.”
How do you clean makeup brushes?

Before you start cleaning, it helps to know what your brushes are made of, since synthetic and natural bristles need slightly different care. Vosburg breaks down those two most common types of brushes below.

Synthetic brushes: Many makeup brushes, especially foundation and lip brushes, are made with synthetic fibers. Because they’re typically used with liquid and cream products, they can hold onto oily buildup that’s tough to remove. A simple soap works well here, since it breaks down oils quickly and gets synthetic bristles clean without much effort.Natural hair brushes: Powder and eyeshadow brushes are often made with natural hair. These bristles are prone to staining from pigmented products like blush, but discoloration is normal and doesn’t mean the brush isn’t clean. Because natural hair can dry out over time, use a moisturizing soap (like a bar soap you may use on your body) or cleaner to keep the bristles soft and healthy.

Synthetic brushes: Many makeup brushes, especially foundation and lip brushes, are made with synthetic fibers. Because they’re typically used with liquid and cream products, they can hold onto oily buildup that’s tough to remove. A simple soap works well here, since it breaks down oils quickly and gets synthetic bristles clean without much effort.

Natural hair brushes: Powder and eyeshadow brushes are often made with natural hair. These bristles are prone to staining from pigmented products like blush, but discoloration is normal and doesn’t mean the brush isn’t clean. Because natural hair can dry out over time, use a moisturizing soap (like a bar soap you may use on your body) or cleaner to keep the bristles soft and healthy.
Once you know what you’re working with, follow these steps:

Choose your soap. Liquid dish soap or shampoo both work, but Vosburg prefers bar soap for natural hair brushes because it’s effective, non-drying and easy to use. “When cleaning with a bar of soap, I will simply wet the tips of the brush hairs with a bit of lukewarm water and then swirl the brush a few times on the bar of soap.” There are also plenty of effective cleansers on the market made specifically for makeup brushes.Work the soap into a lather. After swirling the brush on the bar or adding soap to the bristles, move it to the palm of your hand or on a silicone cleaning pad and continue swirling until it lathers. If you’re using liquid soap, a pea-size amount in your palm is enough for any size brush since it’s concentrated, says Hart. Gently wipe the brush back and forth through the soap, taking care not to press or bend the bristles too hard. Rinse. Hold the brush with the bristles pointing down and run only the brush hairs under lukewarm water. Hot water can damage the hair and loosen the glue that holds the bristles in place, says Hart. Try to keep water away from the ferrule, the metal piece that connects the bristles to the handle, since that’s where the glue and binders are. Not dunking or soaking your brushes will help reduce shedding and help them last longer, according to Vosburg.Repeat as needed. Continue lathering and rinsing until the water runs clear and the brush is free of makeup.Remove excess water and dry. Gently squeeze the bristles with a microfiber towel to remove excess water, then lay the brush flat to air dry.

Choose your soap. Liquid dish soap or shampoo both work, but Vosburg prefers bar soap for natural hair brushes because it’s effective, non-drying and easy to use. “When cleaning with a bar of soap, I will simply wet the tips of the brush hairs with a bit of lukewarm water and then swirl the brush a few times on the bar of soap.” There are also plenty of effective cleansers on the market made specifically for makeup brushes.

Work the soap into a lather. After swirling the brush on the bar or adding soap to the bristles, move it to the palm of your hand or on a silicone cleaning pad and continue swirling until it lathers. If you’re using liquid soap, a pea-size amount in your palm is enough for any size brush since it’s concentrated, says Hart. Gently wipe the brush back and forth through the soap, taking care not to press or bend the bristles too hard.

Rinse. Hold the brush with the bristles pointing down and run only the brush hairs under lukewarm water. Hot water can damage the hair and loosen the glue that holds the bristles in place, says Hart. Try to keep water away from the ferrule, the metal piece that connects the bristles to the handle, since that’s where the glue and binders are. Not dunking or soaking your brushes will help reduce shedding and help them last longer, according to Vosburg.
Repeat as needed. Continue lathering and rinsing until the water runs clear and the brush is free of makeup.
Remove excess water and dry. Gently squeeze the bristles with a microfiber towel to remove excess water, then lay the brush flat to air dry.
Frequently asked questions

With proper cleaning and care, high quality makeup brushes can last for decades, so you shouldn’t need to replace them often, according to Hart. Still, there are a few signs that it’s time for a replacement. If the glue holding the bristles to the handle starts to loosen, the brush will shed excessively, says Hart. Bristles can also flatten and fray over time, especially if you press too hard on your skin when applying makeup. Either issue means the brush should be replaced.

It’s also worth watching for bristles that break in half, which can signal that the hairs have become damaged from dehydration or overuse, according to Vosburg. Broken bristles can lead to a scratchy or uneven application, so that’s another sign it’s time to swap in a new brush.

Makeup sponges can be cleaned much like brushes, according to Hart. Start by wetting the sponge until it’s fully saturated, then swirl it on a bar of soap until it’s coated and work it into a lather in the palm of your hand, says Vosburg. Give it a few squeezes, then rinse it under warm water until no soap remains. Sponges tend to hold onto a lot of product, so you may need to repeat the lathering and rinsing several times before the water runs clear.

Once it’s clean, squeeze out any excess water and let the sponge air dry completely. Avoid storing sponges in a sealed bag or anywhere without steady airflow, since they retain moisture and can grow bacteria and mold if they can’t dry out, says Hart. “I keep my sponges and puffs in a mesh bag, so they’re constantly being aired out while in storage,” he says.
Powder puffs need to be cleaned just as often as your sponges and brushes to keep bacteria and germs from building up, says Hart.

Start by soaking the puff in warm water, then lather it with bar soap or a makeup brush cleanser. With bar soap, you can swirl the puff on the bar and work it into a lather just as you would a sponge or brush. With liquid soap, place a small amount in the center of the puff, fold it in half like a taco and rub the two sides together, according to Vosburg. Squeeze and rinse the puff under warm water, repeating as needed until it’s clean.
To dry, squeeze out the excess water and lay the puff flat. For even better airflow, set it on a kitchen drying rack or something similar so air can circulate all the way around it, says Hart.

title: A Brief History of Madonna and the VMAs: ‘The House She Helped Build’
summary: Madonna is returning to the VMAs. What is Madonna’s history with the VMAs?
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Where would the MTV Video Music Awards be without Madonna?

Madonna’s name is practically synonymous with the VMAs. She was there from the beginning, rolling around the stage in a wedding dress while performing “Like A Virgin” during the awards show’s 1984 debut.

Over the next four decades, Madonna returned to the VMAs to deliver groundbreaking performances. She’s also made headlines with outrageous antics — like French kissing Britney Spears onstage — and touched fans’ hearts with an emotional tribute to Michael Jackson after the musician’s death in 2009.
Now, the Queen of Pop is poised make a historic return to the 2026 VMAs on Sept. 27 when she performs at the awards show for the first time in 23 years.
Madonna’s performance will kick off the awards show for a record-breaking fifth time, ending her tie with Rihanna, who’s opened the show four times.
Madonna who released her hit album, “Confessions II,” in July, also goes into this year’s VMAs as the most nominated performer.
The singer is “returning to sit on her throne for the night,” NBC News entertainment contributor Chris Witherspoon tells TODAY.com.

“You simply cannot tell the story of the VMAs without telling the story of Madonna. From ‘Like a Virgin’ in 1984, to ‘Vogue’ in 1990, to that unforgettable 2003 performance with Britney Spears, Christina Aguilera and Missy Elliott, Madonna understood the assignment before we even had the phrase,” said Witherspoon.
“Madonna returning to the VMAs doesn’t feel like a comeback to me. It feels like the Queen of Pop returning to the house she helped build,” Witherspoon added.
Ahead of Madonna’s triumphant VMAs return, let’s take a look back at her 10 biggest moments at the awards show.
1) The Wedding Dress Seen Round the World (1984)

Madonna’s audacious performance at the inaugural MTV Video Music Awards in 1984 — she rolled around the stage in a punky ensemble that includes a wedding dress, rosary beads and a “Boy Toy” belt buckle — became her breakout moment.
The raunchy performance, which also included some bumping and grinding, also branded the VMAs as a rebellious alternative to the Grammys and other awards shows.

“MTV could barely fill the seats at the VMAs in year one. By year two, pretty much every act wanted a spot on that stage. Madonna was at the first show in 1984, rolling across the stage in a wedding dress singing ‘Like a Virgin.’ I’d give her a lot of credit for that turnaround,” Jeff Moore, a music marketing strategist, professor, and former touring musician, told TODAY.com.
2) Madonna Expresses Herself (1989)
Madonna returned to the VMAs five years later to deliver one of her finest televised performances when she sang “Express Yourself” with her two backup singers-dancers.

The newly divorced singer — her marriage to Sean Penn officially ended earlier in the year —  began her high-energy, tightly choreographed performance wearing a dark suit before stripping down to a corset.
3) ‘Vogue’ Meets the French Revolution (1990)

The former Material Girl’s breathtaking 1990 performance of “Vogue” was inspired by the French Revolution. Madge as Marie Antoinette? Oh, it worked, right down to her and her dancers’ 18th century-style powdered wigs, heavy white face makeup and corseted gowns.
4) ‘Ray of Light’ with Lenny Kravtiz (1998)
In what’s considered one of the best live performances, Madonna showed off her vocal chops on the soaring “Ray of Light’ with guest guitarist Lenny Kravitz during the 1998 show.
The singer, who kicked off the performance with the Hindu-inspired  “Shanti Ashtangi,” also swept the awards that night, taking home five Moon Man trophies.
5) Madonna Meets Her Drag Impersonators (1999)
The singer was feted the following year by a group of drag queens who wore some of her most memorable looks as they lip-synched and danced to her greatest hits.
“All I have to say is that it takes a real man to fill my shoes!” the singer quipped afterwards.
6) Kissing Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera (2003)
In 2003, Madonna shocked viewers when she took a moment during a throwback performance of “Like A Virgin” to kiss shared her guest performers Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.
Spears and Aguilera donned skimpy wedding dress looks in a fun nod to Madonna’s debut VMAs performance.
7) An Emotional Tribute to Michael Jackson (2009)

Madonna showed off her serious side when she paid an emotional tribute to her late fellow pop icon Michael Jackson at the 2009 VMAs, calling Jackson “one of the greatest talents the world has ever known.”

“His music,” she said in her speech, “had an extra layer of inexplicable magic that didn’t just make you want to dance but actually made you believe you could fly, dare to dream, be anything that you wanted to be.”
She also recalled going to dinner with Jackson years before.

“Later we went back to my house to watch a movie and sat on the couch like two kids, and somewhere in the middle of the movie, his hand snuck over and held mine,” she said. “It felt like he was looking for more of a friend than a romance, and I was happy to oblige. In that moment, he didn’t feel like a superstar. He felt like a human being.”
8) A Surprise Appearance, Motherf-----! (2021)
Decked out out black dominatrix bodysuit and cap, Madonna made a surprise appearance to open the 2021 VMAs.
The singer’s appearance came just after viewers watched a short video telling the story of her arrival in New York City decades before with just $35 to her name.
Madonna then walked out onstage, telling the crowd, “And they said we wouldn’t last. But we’re still here, motherf------!”

title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Babylon,’ Explained by 2 History Professors
summary: Taylor Swift’s new song “Babylon” is about a failed relationship and references a famous city of Mesopotamia. Here’s what to know.
story: Taylor Swift’s new song “Babylon” brings a big historical symbol to describe the arc of one relationship that ends before a person realizes how good it was.
It’s part of four new songs Swift dropped as part of her “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore” album on Sept. 25.

“Babylon” is told in the second person, with Swift singing to directly to “you.” That “you” is described as a man who left home — a “small town,” to be specific. He’s said to be an ambitious “libertine” who later “longs for home.”

When he meets a girl who loves him, it “stopped you cold.” He kept her at arm’s length, though, and kept things “never official.” But in a flash forward during the bridge, Swift sings that “you” seemingly went on to start a family, but he misses the most important parts. She sings about a vignette of a woman hanging Christmas lights with the subject of the song’s son and later calling her mom to say, “It’s not working/ It’s just not worth it if we’re not what he wants.”
That all culminates in an explanation of the song’s chorus, which describes the subject on a train with his “headphones gone,” realizing the song he thought he hated, he actually loves.
“Then that melody is all you want/ You never knew that it was Babylon/ ‘Til it was gone,” Swift sings.

Taken alone, the song implies that Babylon is an idyllic setting, set in the past and something to perpetually long for. But the reference has a storied history. The city is referenced in more than a few pop songs, including a 1998 hit by David Gray and a 2020 song by Lady Gaga.

Wait, What is Babylon?
Babylon was an ancient city located in the middle of what is now Iraq, between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

Amanda Podany, a professsor emeritus of history at California State Polytechnic University, tells TODAY.com Babylon is associated with the idea of ruin. Alexander the Great, as legend has it, razed the city, though Podany says that might not have been the case. Still, the legend persisted.

“There’s plenty of evidence for Babylon continuing to be an important place for hundreds of years after that. But again, that sort of went into the popular consciousness as a metaphor for ruin, as a metaphor for something glorious that that fell,” she says.
Its place in pop culture was potentially solidified in the Bible.

“In the Bible, Babylon gets really bad press,” Lloyd Llewellyn-Jones, professor at the University of Cardiff, tells TODAY.com. “It is the ultimate City of Sin; Babylon is the Mother of Harlots; it is home to the Whore of Babylon, whose reign will usher in Armageddon and bring about the Apocalypse.”
But he says the city was actually one of the most sophisticated in the ancient world.

“It was the first ever metropolis, with an enormous multi-cultural population. It was the centre of arts, literature, culture, and industry. It was New York, Paris, Bangkok, Los Angeles and London rolled into one. There was no city on earth to rival it. Babylon was the Mother of All Cities,” he says.
But Podany doesn’t think the Babylon in this song is associated with sinfulness or ruin.

“She seems to be using it as a stand-in for that place that you didn’t realize was the best until you left it or lost it. So she’s choosing, I think, to not view Babylon as representing its kings (some of whom were, yes, imperialistic and brutal), or its supposed wickedness; she’s looking past all the layers of misunderstanding that have accumulated on the word Babylon,” she said.

In a twist Podany called interesting (and perhaps not intentional), she’s associating Babylon with nostalgia, “in the way ancient Babylonians would have indeed felt about the place 3,000 or 4,000 years ago, perhaps when they were traveling far away.”
She continued, “Babylon would have been remembered as a beloved home.”

title: Why Is Marvel’s ‘Avengers: Endgame’ Being Re-Released With Extra Minutes Of Footage?
summary: What happens in the new footage from Avengers: Endgame? Why is it being re-released? Find out why and what happens.
story: It’s been more than seven years since Marvel’s “Avengers: Endgame” debuted in theaters and (Hulk-) smashed box office numbers, becoming one of the top grossing films of all time.
Now, the film is slated to hit theaters once again on Sept. 25.  This time around, it’s got an estimated four minutes added to the original runtime.

The movie —which united the MCU’s original Avengers Iron Man, Captain America, Hulk, Thor, Black Widow and Hawkeye against supervillain warlord Thanos — marked the conclusion of the first decade of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
So why is it back on the big screen with a smidge of extra footage?
The film’s directors, Anthony and Joe Russo, have described the re-release as “required viewing,” setting up viewers for the future of the “Avengers” franchise.
When and Where Is ‘Avengers Endgame: Encore’ Being Released?
The film — which stars Robert Downey Jr., Scarlett Johansson, Mark Ruffalo and several other big names —  will hit theaters once again on Friday, Sept. 25 under the name “Avengers Endgame: Encore.”

Much like when it was first released, the movie will be offered on standard laser projection and IMAX. It will also be shown on Infinity Vision, a Disney-specific certification badge for premium large format theaters.

Those who catch the movie on IMAX and Infinity Vision will be able to watch an additional sneak peek of the much-awaited next film in the “Avengers” franchise, “Avengers: Doomsday,” which comes out on Dec. 18.
Why Is ‘Avengers Endgame’ Being Re-Released?
The Russo brothers, who directed “Endgame,” have said that this re-released version is necessary to watch ahead of “Doomsday,” of which they are also at the helm.

In an interview with Fandango, Joe Russo explained that the re-release, with its added footage, is the connective tissue that links the previous “Avengers” films to the next chapter — one that will usher in the arrival of new supervillain Doctor Doom, also played by Downey Jr.

“There’s a natural progression from “Endgame” into “Doomsday” which is also inclusive of all the other stories that have been playing out,” Joe Russo told Fandango during an interview at San Diego Comic-Con in July.
Of course, fans will also be able to relive all the shocking twists packed in “Endgame” as well, Joe Russo added.
Anthony Russo also explained that the extra few minutes are expected to include some pretty pivotal moments.
“If you saw ‘Endgame’ when it was originally released, you couldn’t see this coming,” he told Fandango.
What Makes This Re-Release Necessary For The Upcoming MCU Storylines?
The original release of “Endgame” was followed by the introduction of villain Kang the Conquerer in 2021’s television series “Loki.” And he’s a villain that Marvel has since abandoned.
Kang, played by Jonathan Majors, was a time traveler who discovered the existence of the Multiverse, seeking to conquer and rule over them all.

The villain was once poised to succeed Thanos as the new Big Bad of the MCU, with Marvel diving into multiverse plotlines and even going so far as announcing in 2022 that film “Avengers: The Kang Dynasty.” would be the successor to “Endgame.” At the time, Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige had even told fans that the film would hit theaters in May 2025.

Majors appeared in a number of Marvel productions including “Ant Man and the Wasp: Quantumania.” However, he was dropped by the studio after he was convicted by a New York City jury of misdemeanor assault and harassment in 2023.
Majors sent a letter to Feige following his termination. In a 2025 interview with Variety, Majors told the outlet that his letter to the Marvel Studios chief included his appreciation for the role.

“I loved my time at Marvel, and I still love Kang,” Majors said, later telling the outlet that he is “not upset at all.” “I’m watching them. I see what they’re doing and I’m pulling for them. If they need me, they know where I’m at.”

Meanwhile, the MCU pursued a different villain, bringing back Downey Jr., the beloved actor behind Tony Stark/Iron Man, to fulfill the role of Doctor Doom. Feige has said that the decision to pivot came before Majors’ controversy.

“We had started even before what had happened to the actor happened,” Feige said during a 2025 roundtable interview with press. “We had started to realize that Kang wasn’t big enough, wasn’t Thanos, and that there was only one character that could be that, because he was that in the comics for decades and decades.”

title: Sheinelle Jones Gives Maleah Joi Moon a Birthday Present on TODAY That Leaves Her Speechless
summary: Maleah Joi Moon celebrated her 24th birthday with a special gift from Sheinelle Jones.
story: Maleah Joi Moon celebrated her 24th birthday with a special gift from Sheinelle Jones.

On Sept. 25, Moon appeared on TODAY to talk about her role as Deborah Wayne, the free-spirited child of Dwayne Wayne and Whitley Gilbert, on Netflix’s “A Different World” sequel, which premiered Sept. 24.

Moon recalled how Debbie Allen, who produced and directed most of the original “A Different World” and returned for the reboot, recognized her talent on the stage. Moon won a Tony Award for her role in “Hell’s Kitchen,” the Broadway musical based on the life and music of Alicia Keys.
“She came to see the show in previews. So she hopped on it before the wave and I feel like that’s a trend for her. She just has such a beautiful vision for things that are impactful,” Moon said.
Moon celebrated her birthday on Sept. 23, and during the interview, Sheinelle gave Moon a present: a T-shirt of Allen’s 1992 cover from Jet Magazine.
Sheinelle revealed she originally bought the shirt for herself.
“And then I was like, wait, I need to give it to Maleah,” Sheinelle said.
“I was going to cut it and make it cute, but then I remembered that I was interviewing you and I want you to have it,” Sheinelle added.
Moon, whose eyes filled with tears, buried her face into the shirt.
“She means so much to me,” she said of Allen.
“Talk about standing on someone’s shoulders,” said Sheinelle. “You’re literally on her shoulders.”
“It’s perfect. She’s perfect,” Moon said of Allen as she and Sheinelle shared an embrace.
Moon called Allen “so many young Black women’s icon” and described their meeting backstage at “Hell’s Kitchen.”
“I cried,” Moon said, recalling the moment, which was captured in a photo. “She just has such a presence about her that is so warm and direct and comforting.”
“Little did I know she would become this pivotal person in my life instead of just an inspiration,” Moon added.

title: Jenna Shares How She Discovered Dad George W. Bush Broke Off an Engagement
summary: A poor grade on a third-grade math test led to a startling discovering when Jenna Bush Hager was a child.
story: A poor grade on a third-grade math test led to a startling discovering when Jenna Bush Hager was a child.
Jenna shared the oblique way she discovered her father, former President George W. Bush, had previously been engaged to another woman before calling off the wedding.
During their chat on TODAY Sept. 25, Sheinelle Jones and Jenna discussed if they knew anyone who had canceled a wedding, sparked by Oprah Winfrey’s recent comments about trusting one’s intuition.
“My dad actually called off a wedding,” Jenna said. “My dad was engaged, and he called off his wedding. They were really young.”
Jenna had no idea until she earned a bad score on a math test in third grade. When her dad was upset with her, she fired back that he probably did the same thing as a kid.

“He was like, ‘No, I didn’t.’ He took out his memory box that my grandmother had made him, or like kind of a photo album, to show a report card, and I saw a wedding announcement to somebody that wasn’t my mom,” Jenna said.
“I started crying and made it about myself, as a third-grader does,” she added.

Bush got engaged in 1967 to Cathryn Lee Wolfman, a fellow college student at the time. The two were both juniors, Bush at Yale and Wolfman at Rice, according to the Houston Press. An announcement of their engagement ran in the Houston Chronicle on Jan. 1, 1967.
Bush ultimately married Jenna’s mother, former first lady Laura Bush, in 1977. The two are parents to Jenna and her twin sister, Barbara.
“I didn’t realize in that third-grade sort of melodramatic (way), good thing he called it off or we wouldn’t have been here,” Jenna said.
The discussion originated from a clip of Winfrey advising people not to ignore their intuition, posing the example of people going through with a wedding when they know they shouldn’t.
Jenna said she once attended a wedding and could sense her friend reluctantly going through with it. The couple ultimately got divorced years later.
“To be able to able to walk away from something like that, you really do have to listen to yourself,” Jenna said.

title: Brandi Carlile Revisits Her Post About First Time Meeting Dolly Parton — Exactly 10 Years Ago on 9/25
summary: Brandi Carlile recalls meeting Dolly Parton for the first time in 2016 and posting about it on social media on Sept. 25, now Dolly Parton Day, 10 years later.
story: As the country gears up to celebrate Dolly Parton Day on Sept. 25 — aka 9/25, in honor of her classic song “9 to 5” — Brandi Carlile is remembering the first time she met the iconic singer, who died last month at the age of 80.

During a Sept. 25 appearance on TODAY, Carlile was reminded of a Facebook post she shared exactly 10 years ago to the day. On Sept. 25, 2016, she posted a photo with Parton and wrote about meeting the “Jolene” singer.
“Well it finally happened... I met the queen! I have no recollection of what I said but @dollyparton is the greatest preacher the world has seen!” Carlile captioned the photo of them.
“I didn’t know that,” Carlile said when told on TODAY the post was from exactly a decade earlier.
“That was backstage at her concert. I went, bought a ticket, went and saw that show,” she added.
The 11-time Grammy winner would go on to forge a relationship with Parton, explaining she had always longed to meet her.
“It’s like every little girl’s dream that ever plays a guitar and sings a song to grow up and find a way to meet Dolly Parton, so I was pretty on mission early on to meet Dolly,” she said.
The two would eventually work together at a music festival in Newport, Rhode Island, in 2019, an experience that Carlile said was made all the better by Parton.
“I got tasked with, or the gift rather, of getting to curate the first all-female headlining set at the Newport Folk Festival, which is just like a history making place,” she said.

“It’s one of the most important festivals I think in in U.S. history, and I just knew we couldn’t do it without Dolly, and so that’s how I became I think close with Dolly, was through her deciding to come and grace the stage of that festival,” she added.
The “Party of One” singer recalled Parton had a very commanding presence.
“She was like half humor. She was formidable, and she was faithful,” she said.
She said Parton arrived at the festival with five-inch heels and fingernails.
“I was so taken aback when I saw that vision of her, and I realized the gravity of the situation, and my eyes started welling up with tears, despite myself, in the dressing room,” Carlile recalled.

“And I just said, ‘I’m really nervous.’ And we were her backing band, and I was like, ‘I feel maybe I’ve bitten off more than I can chew.’ And she says, ‘Well, darling, we need to do something about that,’ and just took my face in her hands and prayed with me, and it was like transformative,” she added.

Carlile credited Parton’s ability to connect with people with her upbringing. Parton was born in Locust Ridge in rural Tennessee. One of 12 children, she was raised in a one-room cabin on the banks of the Little Pigeon River.

“I think it has a lot to do with her growing up poor, and her role in her family, and knowing how to take care of people, but knowing how to lighten the mood, and her faith that permeated everything that she did,” Carlile said.
New York City, New Orleans and Portland, Oregon are among the cities celebrating Dolly Parton Day, but the honors for the beloved singer don’t stop with one day.

Nashville’s airport authority board unanimously voted earlier this month to begin the process to rename the airport after her. Her estate also announced a two-day festival called Dollyfest set for 2027 as a tribute to her.

Drivers in Ohio can also purchase a license plate with Parton’s image to support Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library in the state, while American Airlines will change its daily flight from Dallas to Nashville to flight 925. Aer Lingus is also modifying its flight from Dublin to Nashville to make it flight 95.

title: ‘America’s Got Talent’ Winner Nene Royal Says She ‘Never Expected to Actually Win’
summary: Nene Royal speaks about winning America’s Got Talent and what’s next for her in an interview with TODAY.com.
story: Nene Royal is on her way to being rock royalty.

The 16-year-old singer and guitarist from Thailand won the 21st season of “America’s Got Talent” on Sept. 23, capping a season in which she wowed viewers and the judges with her blistering guitar play and fierce vocals.
After host Terry Crews revealed her name as the winner, Royal fell onto the stage in disbelief.
“I was so shocked because the moment just went completely black,” she told TODAY.com the day after the win.
“There’s so, so many emotions that at once, shock or happiness, everything, and my body just reacted before my brain did,” she added.
Royal already has her eyes on what looks like a bright future.

“My next thing for me is doing some my own songs, or making (an) album, and also making some tours,” she said while noting she’d like to collaborate with acts who’ve influenced and inspired her, including Avenged Sevenfold, Metallica, Limp Bizkit, The Warning and Linkin Park, with whom she performed during the finale.

Royal, who defeated magician Geno Ploege when they were down to the final two acts, says she never felt confident she would win. She earned the Golden Buzzer to advance to the finals after she performed Soundgarden’s “Black Hole Sun,” which told her maybe she did indeed have the chops to win it all.

“I just focused on each round and tried to make every performance better than the last time,” she said. “Maybe after the Golden Buzzer, I started thinking like, ‘Wow, maybe I really do have a chance,’ but I still never expected to actually win.”
Royal also points to the nurturing nature of judges Howie Mandel, Sofia Vergara, Mel B and Simon Cowell, who were kind to her when the cameras weren’t rolling during the competition.
“(They) just came to me and said like, ‘I’m very proud of you and just be yourself and you know your life is going to be changed,’” she said.
Royal, who started playing guitar at age 7, says rock music has proven to be a natural fit for her.

“I think it is the energy, that freedom (of) rock music. When I play rock, especially on guitar, because I feel like I can really be myself and express everything that I’m feeling, because I love the powerful sounds and the guitar solos and the energy that you get from performing it live,” she said.
“And the first time I really got into rock, I was like, ‘Yeah, this is me. This is why I wanted to play.’”
It’s a long way from Thailand for Royal, who grasps the magnitude of her accomplishment winning “AGT,” while also feeling gratitude for the support of her loved ones.

“It’s been such a crazy journey, let’s say that, for all of us, especially coming all the way from Thailand to America. I’m really grateful, and they’ve been there with me through everything,” she said.

title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Pink Clouding’ Is About an Overdue Apology. Read the Lyrics
summary: What is the meaning of Taylor Swift’s new song Pink Clouding on The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore? Read the lyrics.
story: Taylor Swift is offering up an apology in her new track “Pink Clouding.”
The song is one of four new songs on the pop icon’s recently announced “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,” out now.

“Pink Clouding” is seemingly about the song’s narrator taking ownership of the ways she let someone else down. She admits it from the first verse. The two met in an idyllic setting. Shades of the color pink are used to show just how idyllic — magenta, fuchsia and rosewood.
Then, Swift drops the bomb, shattering the rose-colored vista: “I was a liar,” though, “neither of us knew it at the time.”
The song describes a case of one person leading the person on while they’re both in a rose-colored dreamscape. Swift says it felt good, “letting you want me ... to make promises.”
Part of the problem was what came before her relationship with this man. Swift says they met at a “cursed time” for her when she was coming off a bad relationship.
“He cut me crimson, bled me dry/ He crossеd my heart, I hoped to die/ ripped all my orchids from the vine,” she sings.
Swift “said I was fine,” but likely wasn’t. The bridge is a straight-up apology.
“And the way I treated you, you never deserved it/ And I swear to God, to this day/ I wake up scared that I left scars on a good person,” she sings.
“Years later, I still wonder how to tell you sorry,” she continues in the bridge.

In the chorus, she also sings she was “gray rocking when the arrow hit.” Gray rocking is a tactic used to disarm manipulative behavior. Instead of reacting, you shut down. This could be a holdover from her past relationship. (“Patient Zero” is notably about being the first person “infected” by a toxic person.) Or, it could be a way for her to describe not being moved when the “arrow” — as in Cupid’s — hit.
She describes the way the relationship ended, which seems abrupt. She “didn’t wanna let you down,” so she “left you up there on a pink cloud.”
“I hope you landed safely on the ground,” she sings later.
Swift first revealed to fans that new music was coming sooner than expected on Sept. 22 when she announced that her new single “Patient Zero” would be out Sept. 25.
She gave Swifties just one day to process the news before she shared that the single was one of four songs on the extended edition of her 12th album, which was released in October 2025.
She said those songs were “born out of pure gratitude for your exuberance for and celebration of the album we made.”
Along with “Pink Clouding” and “Patient Zero,” the new release also includes “Babylon” and “Cleveland!”

title: Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ Is About a Toxic Relationship She ‘Walked Away’ From
summary: What is the meaning of Taylor Swift’s new song “Patient Zero” on “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore?” Read the lyrics.
story: “Patient Zero,” one of Taylor Swift’s four new songs released as part of her “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,” opens with an evocative and melancholy violin, setting the tone for the rest of the song.
The song is structured like a one-sided phone call, with Swift’s character speaking to a caller about a man they both knew — and warning her about him.
“I’ve gotta be honest, I’ve been expecting your call,” she sings.

Swift calls herself “patient zero,” meaning the first person infected by the “toxins” from the subject of the song. Because she dated him before the new person, she’s trying to wake the caller up to the truth.
“If you’re sick of him I got you, I was patient zero,” she says.

Swift describes a relationship with all the hallmarks of love bombing: He burst into your life like “fireworks” and says “I love you” first. But, according to the lyrics, he also cheats, parties and gets bored.
Swift speak-sings more details about this man’s sins and how they were at first disguised. Missteps include:

Charm: “I know he charmed your family and friends/ And you thought it’s ‘cause he loves you/ But it’s ‘cause he loves how everybody else loves him”Using his partner for clout: “I know it seems like he shines so bright/ But he’s bathing in your reflected light/ On a free solo social climb”
Charm: “I know he charmed your family and friends/ And you thought it’s ‘cause he loves you/ But it’s ‘cause he loves how everybody else loves him”
Using his partner for clout: “I know it seems like he shines so bright/ But he’s bathing in your reflected light/ On a free solo social climb”
Swift says she “said all of this to his face” and eventually “walked away.”
This is a departure from other songs on “The Life of a Showgirl,” which is largely inspired by her happy relationship with her husband Travis Kelce and her experience on “The Eras Tour.”
Swift will release the music video for “Patient Zero” at the VMAs on Sept. 27, where Swift will also be the inaugural recipient of the first-ever Artist Director Honors.

“The Life of a Showgirl” was Swift’s reflection coming out of her career-retrospective “Eras” world tour. Written and produced with Max Martin and Shellback while on the tour, the album explores the highs and lows of fame, and what it means to fall in love with all eyes on you. The upbeat pop record broke first-week sales records, and singles “The Fate of Ophelia” and “Opalite” topped charts.

Swift has characteristically kept herself busy in the last year. She became one of the youngest people inducted in the Songwriters Hall of Fame, released “I Knew It, I Knew You” for Disney’s “Toy Story 5,” and married Travis Kelce in a massive wedding at New York City’s storied Madison Square Garden.

title: Is Taylor Swift’s ‘Cleveland!’ About Who We Think It Is? Lyrics Say Definitely
summary: What is Taylor Swift’s “Cleveland!” about? Read the song lyrics and find out exactly how they are a reference to Travis Kelce.
story: Taylor Swift wants us all to know she’s found the love of her life.
One of four songs released as part of “The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore,” “Cleveland!” proves another saccharine sweet love story overflowing with references to her now husband Travis Kelce.
In classic Swift fashion, he’s never mentioned by name, and she’s famous for rarely confirming the inspiration for her songs. But this song has a pretty clear source.

The song’s narrator consistently sings about feelings of insecurity, both from herself and from the world at large, opening with the sentiment, “She’s not as hot as she was.” But the instrumentals, driven by energetic drums and uplifting piano, keep things light leading into the big twist brought on by the chorus: She only really cares what one person thinks.
“My baby likes what he likes,” she sings.

She sings about how he’s already taken her to Cleveland and shown her “the Heights.” Kelce is from Westlake, Ohio, near Cleveland Heights, which inspired the name of his podcast with brother Jason Kelce, “New Heights.”

This is the second time Swift has referenced “Heights” on a song. The first came on the original “Life of a Showgirl” tracklist, “Wood,” an innuendo pop song with a chorus that includes the line, “New Heights of manhood.”
By the end of the song, she’s singing about more than just visiting someone’s hometown — she’s preparing to walk down the aisle.
“Now I’m wearin’ white, so hate all you like/ This is the love of my life,” she sings to close out the song.
Swift and Kelce married on July 3 at Madison Square Garden after getting engaged in August 2025.
